paragraphs: As a lifelong resident of Antioch, I’ve spent more than 20 years in public service working to make our community safer, stronger, and more connected. I previously served on the Antioch City Council and had the honor to lead the Antioch School Board as President, helping guide decisions that affect our families and children’s future. More than 25 years in the financial industry, along with leadership across local government, made clear to me what residents need: sound planning, responsible budgeting, transparency that leads to results you can feel every day.

Beyond elected office, I remain deeply engaged in community service. I currently lead the Celebrate Antioch Foundation as President, serve as a Director on the Antioch Schools Education Foundation, as well as serving on the Chamber of Commerce, Antioch Women’s Club, and Antioch Historical Society. These roles reflect my commitment to strengthening partnerships and ensuring Antioch’s promise is fulfilled for every neighborhood.

If elected to the Antioch City Council, I will focus on four priorities: public safety, economic growth, community pride and accountability, and revitalizing downtown. I will advocate for data-driven public safety strategies; pursue policies that encourage investment and job creation; and promote city government that listens. I will address blight and vacant properties with consistent enforcement and replace neglect with opportunity. Finally, I will work to accelerate downtown revitalization, supporting increased commercial activity and walkable public spaces.
We can’t accept stagnancy. I will bring urgency, measurable goals, and accountability for a safer, stronger, more vibrant Antioch. Choose Joy!
As your District 1 Councilwoman, I’ve kept my promise to fight for working families, safer neighborhoods, and our most vulnerable residents.

I fought to bring more than $10 million in outside funding to the Department of Community Resources to support violence prevention and Antioch’s Youth Services Network—including the city’s S.O.A.R. internship program, which has already put 91 young adults facing real barriers into paid apprenticeships and a path toward a career.
I fought for $4 million in CalVIP grants to launch the Peace Fellowship, connecting residents at the center of gun violence with mentorship, wraparound resources, and accountability.

Because District 1 has felt the brunt of our homelessness crisis, I fought to secure a $34.9 million grant for permanent supportive housing—and I’ll continue pushing the city to invest in sustainable, long-term solutions to address our unhoused population.
I fought for renters, helping pass the Just Cause Eviction ordinance to stop unfair displacement by landlords.
I’ve called out vacant, blighted commercial properties that block economic development and fought to hold absentee landlords accountable.

Residents in the Sycamore area asked me for a long-term commitment to their safety. I fought harder than anyone on the council for the Sycamore Square police substation, bringing police and community resources to a neighborhood that has long been overlooked.
There’s more work ahead, and I’m not backing down. I’m asking for your vote, so I can keep fighting for an Antioch that works for all of us.
https://www.tamishaforantiochd1.com/

For more than 16 years, I have proudly called Antioch home, where I have built my career and dedicated myself to serving our community. As a business executive and Vice President of Human Resources for a multi-state healthcare organization, I oversee complex operations, strategic planning, labor relations, compliance, and workforce management for thousands of employees. Every day, I make thoughtful, accountable decisions that balance fiscal responsibility with the needs of people.

My commitment to public service extends beyond my profession. I have served as President of the Antioch Rotary Club, Chair of the Antioch Crime Prevention Commission, a member of the Antioch Unified School District Career Technical Education Committee, and a board member of the Antioch Public Schools Education Foundation and Delta Learning Center. These experiences have strengthened my commitment to collaboration, transparency, and delivering meaningful results for our community.

Antioch deserves leadership focused on practical solutions, accountability, and results. I will prioritize improving public safety, attracting new businesses and quality jobs, supporting youth and families, maintaining clean and safe neighborhoods, and ensuring responsible, compassionate solutions for our unhoused population. I believe we can strengthen our local economy, revitalize our commercial corridors, and make Antioch a destination where families and businesses choose to invest.

I am running for City Council because I believe Antioch’s greatest opportunities are still ahead. With proven executive leadership, community service, and a commitment to listening to and working with residents, I will bring integrity, experience, and a results-driven approach to City Hall.
Antioch has made real progress over the past several years—but our work isn’t done.
Economic Development

Creating jobs, attracting shopping and restaurants, and ensuring balanced growth are among my top priorities for District 4. I support responsible growth that brings jobs, housing, and the infrastructure our neighborhoods need to thrive. I also pushed for the city’s Just Cause Eviction ordinance and stronger protections against landlord retaliation.
Fiscal Responsibility

During two years of budget tightening, I fought to protect essential services while keeping Antioch’s finances on solid ground. When federal gridlock threatened city funding, I traveled to Washington to lobby federal agencies and elected officials to secure additional funding, including funds to address chronic flooding. I also fought for a dedicated grant writer because fiscal responsibility means competing for every tax dollar Antioch can get.
Clean Neighborhoods

Blighted, abandoned commercial properties hurt our community and local economy. I’ve fought to hold absentee commercial landlords accountable and put vacant buildings back into productive use. I also continue to support transitional housing and outreach programs helping move unhoused residents off our streets and into stable housing.

Great leaders listen. I’ve built my career by bringing people together, hearing their concerns, and solving problems collaboratively. As your District 4 councilwoman, I’ll continue to do so. I’m asking for your support so we can keep Antioch moving forward.
I am Matty Alappat and I am running for Antioch City Council, District 4, to help build a safer, cleaner and more prosperous community for all of us.
For the last 15 years I have worked in the software industry, solving tough problems and leading successful initiatives. I am ready to bring that same practical approach to City Council.

I was fortunate to be raised by a mom who was a science teacher and a dad who worked in banking. They taught me that success is built on hard work, integrity, respect for others, and giving back to your community — values I still live by today.
If elected, my top priority will be public safety. I will make sure the police have the resources required to fight crime and protect our neighborhoods.

We also have to take better care of our city. That means investing in city’s infrastructure, revitalizing downtown, maintaining clean pet-friendly public spaces and bringing in new businesses and good-paying jobs.

Housing policies must be carefully planned to fit existing neighborhoods and should only move forward where our infrastructure can truly support them. We will partner with nonprofits to help unhoused individuals achieve long-term stability and self-sufficiency, while also focusing on short-term transitional housing options.
Antioch deserves leadership that brings people together, spends taxpayer dollars wisely, and gets results. I am committed to making Antioch a place we can all be proud of.
I look forward to earning your support.

I’m running for Antioch City Council because I believe our city needs leaders who are willing to do the work–not just talk about it. Having been raised in Antioch and living here for 30 years, I have a connection to this community and knowledge of how our city has grown, changed, and the challenges we face today.

I have regularly attended City Council meetings, studied budgets, development proposals, infrastructure projects, and policy decisions. I have asked questions, listened to residents, and worked to offer solutions. Antioch deserves leadership that is engaged and accountable.

My priorities are restoring fiscal responsibility, strengthening public safety, growing Antioch’s economy, and attracting businesses that create local jobs. City government must live within its means, spend taxpayer dollars wisely, and make decisions that encourage investment rather than drive it away. A local economy creates opportunities for residents, improves city services, and builds a future.

As a District 4 resident and involved Antioch community member, I understand the importance of thoughtful planning, growth, and accountable government. City Hall should focus on solutions instead of political rhetoric. Every decision should be measured by one standard: does it improve the quality of life for Antioch residents?

I will continue listening to our community, making decisions based on facts, and ensuring taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly. My goal is to restore trust in local government, support economic growth, and build an Antioch where families and businesses can thrive.
I respectfully ask for your vote for Antioch City Council District 4.

For the past 10 years, I have proudly called Brentwood home. I’m running for City Council, District 2, because our community deserves leadership that listens, serves with integrity, and puts residents first. As a small business owner, I understand hard work, fiscal responsibility, and the need for a strong local economy. I believe every resident, family, and business deserves to be treated fairly and with respect. My priorities are strengthening public safety, supporting our agricultural heritage and local businesses, and ensuring responsible, well-planned growth. I believe leadership is about service and accountability to our community. I will listen, be transparent, and work collaboratively to find practical solutions. Together, we can preserve the values that make Brentwood a wonderful place to live while planning wisely for future generations. Learn more at tammyforbrentwood.com

Brentwood is a special place my three-generation family calls home – my parents, my wife and I, with four children in BUSD. I have been active in this community for several years, and I’m proud to serve as the Chairperson of Brentwood’s Planning Commission, fighting tirelessly to preserve the small-town community charm in alignment with our city’s General Plan.

I have been an active participant in shaping our community by serving on such committees as the Land Use and Development Committee, IME School Site Council, Measure B Oversight Committee, TRANSPLAN, and many more.

My Planning Commission votes speak for themselves; supporting projects like Costco, Streets of Brentwood building improvements, and the cap on gas stations, car washes, and drive-thrus. Maintaining a family-friendly environment and a focus on the future of Brentwood are at the heart of every decision I make.
Today’s leadership will have rippling effects for decades to come. Join me on this journey to amplify the origins of our great community. I’ll close with a quote:
“A society grows great when old men plant trees whose shade they know they shall never sit in.”
I would be honored to receive your vote.
Brandforbrentwood.com

I am running for Brentwood City Council, District 2, to bring my experience, community service, and practical problem-solving to City Hall. I am a 20-year Brentwood resident, married father of three, Senior Software Engineer, and community volunteer committed to serving our community.

My priorities are improving traffic, strengthening infrastructure, revitalizing Brentwood, protecting public safety, supporting local businesses, growing our local economy, and making sure growth is matched by the infrastructure and services our residents need.
I believe every resident deserves to be heard. I will communicate openly, work collaboratively, and focus on practical solutions that improve the quality of life for our families and neighborhoods.

I currently serve our community as a Brentwood Trustee with the Contra Costa Mosquito & Vector Control District, a Commissioner on the Contra Costa County Airport Land Use Commission, a School Site Council Parent Member, and in other local community leadership roles.

Through these roles, I have worked with people from many backgrounds on issues involving public health, neighborhoods, schools, transportation, land use, and community priorities. These experiences have taught me the importance of teamwork, practical solutions, and responsible use of limited resources.
After 20 years of calling Brentwood home, I would be honored to continue serving our community on the City Council and to serve the residents of District 2 and all of Brentwood.
I respectfully ask for your vote on November 3, 2026.

The decisions we make today will shape our neighborhoods, local economy, infrastructure, and quality of life for years to come. I’m running for Brentwood City Council because I want to help strengthen our community while preparing Brentwood for the future.

For years, Brentwood has entrusted me with making important decisions on behalf of our community. As a former Brentwood Union School District Board Trustee, I guided our school district through the pandemic, made responsible financial decisions, and advocated for public education at the federal level. I also served as Chair of the Brentwood Parks & Recreation Commission, where I championed inclusive recreation and accessibility for residents of all abilities.

Professionally, I work with leaders to solve complex challenges by listening first, understanding the facts, and finding practical solutions that improve healthcare quality and affordability. My husband and I are the co-founders of Miles for Mayo, a nonprofit that hosts an annual 5K at Veterans Park, bringing hundreds of people of all ages together to promote movement, build community, and strengthen the connections that make Brentwood special.

Throughout my career and public service, I’ve learned the best decisions come from listening, evaluating the facts, and considering different perspectives. That’s the approach I’ll bring to the Brentwood City Council. I’ll come prepared, respect different viewpoints, and make thoughtful decisions that strengthen our community.
I would be honored to receive your vote for Brentwood City Council.
www.stephanieforbrentwood.com

My name is Sheree Shannon, and I am running for City Council, District 4. As a proud Brentwood resident for 23 years, a mom of three, and a grandmother of four, I’ve managed my husband’s remodeling business for 36 years while also serving as a Realtor, author, and co-founder of Rise Up, inspiring women to pursue their purpose.

Leading by example, I am pursuing my purpose to positively impact our city as I partner with the Mayor and City Council to create an environment where every resident can thrive while feeling safe and connected.
Public safety is non-negotiable. When tragedy strikes, response time matters. We must ensure our emergency services are fully staffed and have what they need to keep us safe.

Smart city planning requires strong infrastructure while protecting the character of our existing neighborhoods. We need responsible growth that strengthens our local economy, expands housing opportunities, provides quality jobs, and preserves the Brentwood we love. Moving Brentwood forward will take fiscal responsibility, integrity, and strategic planning, and I am prepared to bring those qualities.

My experience managing a successful business for 36 years through economic downturns, changing markets, and the pandemic has prepared me to make sound decisions, solve complex problems, and lead with confidence. I will bring that same proven leadership and practical experience to serving Brentwood.
With dedication, laser focus, and hard work, Brentwood will remain strong, safe, and a place we are all proud to call home. I respectfully ask for your vote.
My name is Holley Bishop-Mello, and I am asking for your vote for Brentwood City Council District 4.

I was born and raised in Brentwood and am a proud mother, Human Resources professional, and small business owner. For more than 25 years, I helped organizations solve problems, build consensus, and serve people. Today, I work in agriculture and understand firsthand the challenges facing local businesses, working families, and our farming community.

My involvement in our community comes from a simple belief: the people of Brentwood deserve to be heard. I have stood alongside residents, small business owners, families, and city employees to advocate for the issues that affect their everyday lives.

I have advocated for fair wages for city employees and emergency responders, safe drinking water, and greater parental involvement and transparency in our schools. When residents felt their voices weren’t being heard, I stood with them and spoke up. That experience strengthened my belief that elected officials have a responsibility to listen – even when they disagree.

As your Council member, I will support public safety, responsible growth, small businesses, agriculture, and fiscal responsibility. I will work to protect Brentwood’s quality of life while considering the financial impact local government decisions have on our residents and businesses. I will ask questions, listen to residents, and make decisions based on what is best for our community.
Brentwood’s future should be shaped by the people who live here – not outside interests.
It would be an honor to earn your vote.
HolleyForBrentwood.com

I have been a proud Clayton resident and homeowner since 2002, raising two children here, alongside my husband, Chris. With a degree in Business Management, I am a Senior Commercial Property Manager with 30 years’ experience working with large property and facility budgets, project management, planning, and property development and redevelopment. I have extensive experience working with city governments and local agencies throughout the Bay Area. I have held a real estate license since 1998 and am certified with the Building Owners and Managers Association as a Real Property Administrator. I write, review, and operate contracts every day while mentoring a large staff and many vendors. My work helps to grow companies and property portfolios. My pledge is to bring civility, accountability, and accessibility to the Council and to use my work-life experience, together with my love of Clayton, to champion safety, education, and infrastructure enhancements throughout the city, and to build revenue to keep Clayton prosperous. I would be honored to have your vote.

Throughout my career, I’ve dedicated myself to caring for individuals and have spent my years in Clayton serving this community. As a nurse and healthcare leader, I have held management, supervisory, pediatric special-needs, and care-management positions, earning recognition from Today’s Nurse for my advocacy and leadership in patient care. These experiences have taught me to listen attentively, ask tough questions, and make complex decisions when the stakes are high.

Currently, I serve on the Clayton Planning Commission, where I was Chair in 2025 and Vice Chair in 2024. In these roles, I helped guide thoughtful growth that preserves our small-town character. Additionally, I serve on the Clayton Community Library Foundation Board and volunteer at events such as Clayton Cleans Up, the Art & Wine Festival, the Fourth of July parade, and Oktoberfest.

I bring extensive experience in managing budgets, ensuring regulatory compliance, and being accountable for my decisions. I am not a political insider; I am committed to working on behalf of all Clayton residents.

My decision to run for office is inspired by the need to address significant challenges facing Clayton, including a limited budget, state housing mandates, aging infrastructure, fire safety, and ensuring residents have a seat at the table.
www.mariaforclayton.com
I intend to serve the citizens of Clayton to maintain a fiscally responsible and careful balance between progress and keeping intact the charming character and landscape of the town that we all love.
As a retired Lieutenant Colonel, my 28 years in the U.S. Army Reserve in planning and operations gave me the leadership skills to serve the public with dedication.

For more than 10 years, I taught Chemistry at the University of Florida. I worked on food safety and environmental projects, and I currently sit on the Board of Directors of the North American Pesticide Residue Workshop.
I am a 24-year Clayton resident; married for 50+ years; have raised two children; and have two grandchildren.

My commitments to Clayton include an appointment to the Clayton Planning Commission, serving on the Trails and Landscape Committee, and continuing as a community volunteer and Senior Advisor to the CBCA Clayton Oktoberfest.
Dedicated service is a part of me, and I hope that you will consider my becoming a member of your Clayton City Council.
I would be honored to have your vote.
Thank you.

I ran for office in 2022 because we needed to examine our finances, assess our priorities and start addressing longstanding issues that had been deferred. The result of this hard work led to a number of outstanding results over the last four years, including an in-depth scrutiny and review of the City’s finances, contracts, vendor agreements, investment strategy, master fee schedule, budget review, GHAD assessment, infrastructure projects and years of planning the library refresh project.

We now have a deeper understanding of where the City stands financially and more importantly the direction it needs to go. Because of the hard work of staff and the Budget & Audit committee, on which I have served since 2023, the City finally has an accurate picture of its finances and is able to forecast and budget accordingly.

I am running for re-election because I want to ensure that we continue to move forward, address our needs, and not fall into the old patterns of ignoring priorities and longstanding issues. I plan on continuing to shine a light on the reality of our situation while keeping the City moving forward so that we do not lose sight of our potential and bright future ahead.

It has been an honor to serve as your elected Concord City Treasurer for the past nine years, and I respectfully ask for your vote for reelection to continue protecting the City’s financial resources with integrity, transparency, and sound fiscal management.

As your Treasurer, I have worked diligently to ensure Concord’s investment portfolio is managed with safety, liquidity, and investment returns as the highest priorities. During my tenure, I have supported a thoughtful investment strategy that modestly extended investment maturities, when appropriate, to improve earnings while maintaining the City’s strong financial safeguards. As a result, the City’s current performance outperformed its benchmark, helping maximize returns on public funds while preserving security.

I regularly review the City’s investment policy and quarterly investment reports, work closely with our professional investment advisors, and help ensure the City maintains the liquidity needed to meet its financial obligations.

My background in banking, commercial lending, investment management, and public service provides the experience needed to responsibly oversee taxpayer dollars. I believe every public dollar should be invested carefully, transparently, and with accountability.
If reelected, I will continue to support responsible financial policies, safeguard public funds, and work to ensure Concord remains financially strong for today and for future generations.
I would be honored to continue serving the residents of Concord as your City Treasurer and respectfully ask for your vote.
B.S. UC Davis, City/Environmental Planning

As a lifelong Concord resident, and your Councilmember, my experienced Leadership, including serving as Mayor, has allowed me to guide Concord through recessions, recovery, and major periods of change and challenges.

I’ve been working on your priorities – improving roads, increasing public safety and reducing homelessness, budget stabilization fund helping city finances during economic downturns; Volunteer programs saving city money, and new housing downtown, and free downtown concerts.

Implemented more than $120 million in road repaving: most major roads completed and starting neighborhood streets. Enhanced public safety: updated technology and equipment improving police officers response and more effectively solving crimes, improved dispatch services, body worn cameras, increased officer recruitment and retention. Homelessness has been reduced with County mental health partnerships, outreach teams and nonprofit housing organizations.

My priorities for you and the city are: maintain public safety, repave more roads, address neighborhood speeding/cut through traffic, improve traffic flow on major roads, reduce homelessness, protect neighborhoods, ensure Base Reuse plan has community input and review, maintains 100-yard buffer to existing neighborhoods, support senior/youth activities, new downtown housing opportunities, engage property owners to improve older retail areas, and keep Concord financially strong.

I’ve worked to keep our city financially stable, protect essential services, support local businesses, and make sure residents receive practical results from City Hall. I’ll continue listening, working hard, and serving with honesty, respect, steady and transparent leadership. I would be honored to receive your support and vote.
www.VoteforLaura.net email: [email removed] ph/txt: 925-250-8532

Concord is my home, and I have a deep appreciation for our city. I built a small business on Clayton Road and chose this city for me and my family’s future because of that appreciation and because I see its potential.

For years I’ve managed public money responsibly as Finance Manager for West County Wastewater District, where I handle budgets, scrutinize spending, monitor payroll, and above all protect the taxpayers’ money. That isn’t a talking point, it’s my calling and my job.

Concord needs greater and fresh accountability. The Concord Naval Weapons Station redevelopment is the largest project in our city’s history, bringing thousands of homes, jobs, and parks. Done right, it will ease our housing shortage and grow our economy. Done carelessly, it may burden taxpayers for generations. I’ll hold the master developer to every promise, demand transparency, and always put the interests of our city first. This is a project that will last for decades and requires long-range leadership, vision, and financial discipline.

My priorities are practical: housing families can afford, traffic that respects your time, safe neighborhoods, and infrastructure we can trust. Most of all, I’ll listen. The biggest decisions shouldn’t be made without you, and I’ll fight for real community input at every step.
I’m not a career politician. I’m a neighbor who shows up, listens, and does the work. I’d be honored to earn your vote and put my experience to work for District 1.

I am running for a position with the City of Concord as a District 1 City Council Member. My slogan is “People, Pets, and Community”. I have spent my adult life doing my best to make my community a better place for people and pets. I have been a psychologist (now retired) since 1994, both in private practice and as Assistant Professor at Oregon Health Sciences University. I have worked as a neuropsychologist with brain injured individuals, people with addictions of all types, couples going through infertility treatment, and individuals and couples needing general therapy.

Animals have also been my lifelong passion. I have always had dogs and cats. Since moving back to California, I have volunteered for Joybound (previously ARF), Contra Costa Animal Services as a foster, and currently, I am a volunteer for Stitch in Time Animal Rescue (STAR), running the spay/neuter program.

I also have an extensive real estate background focusing on home restoration. As a Concord City Council member, I will have more of an opportunity to demonstrate what I can do for community; whether it is addressing the animals being dumped on the streets, the homeless situation, promoting low- and moderate-income housing, or finding a resolution for the Concord Navel Weapons property. As you can see, I am truly passionate about people, pets, and my community, and have the drive, experience, and business savvy to make changes happen. It’s time for a change!
My name is Robyn Kuslits, and I’m running to be your District 3 representative for Concord’s City Council.

I’m running because I believe our community deserves a local government that stands up for their safety, listens to their concerns, and fights for their needs. Concord claims to be a city where families come first, yet from my window I see the immigration court and am reminded daily that federal agents are standing by to tear my community’s families apart.
As a veteran, non-profit leader, law school graduate, and substitute teacher I know what it means to serve and understand the needs of our most vulnerable neighbors. You can count on Kuslits!

As your council member, I will work with everyone from our schools to our neighboring cities and within our local, regional, and state agencies to strengthen safety and trust from our streets to our courthouses. That means protecting every resident regardless of immigration status, defending affordable housing, bringing back just cause rent control, clean parks and public bathrooms, safe streets and sidewalks, and building community.
For more information about me and my stance on important issues, please visit www.votekuslits.com or email me at [email removed].

I am proud and honored to live in such a wonderful place, where my grandmother once lived down the street and my grandfather served as a Concord police officer. Our district has some struggles, but I believe we can solve them together. I look forward to meeting you, and humbly ask for your vote.

As a mother of two young children, lifelong volunteer, and active community member, my goal as your city councilmember is to provide greater access to resources that improve quality of life, combat the cost of living crisis, and strive for equity for our diverse and lower-income neighborhoods. District 3 is the gateway to Concord, and the amount of traffic and commerce throughout our district must be adequately met with quality roads, pedestrian safety measures, and economic development. I’ll advocate for these issues as I did with city staff, leading to installation of 3 crosswalks across busy Market/Meadow Streets. Our district is unique as home to tenants, homeowners, the Community Youth Center, and commercial business areas. Join me in uplifting these people and spaces by connecting one to the other with safe roads, thriving properties, and community hubs we can create. I’ll take my experience identifying resources for families and strive to provide more where need exists – especially for women & children, tenants, small business, the elderly, and the disenfranchised. I volunteer at school and in our community, support my firefighter husband’s demanding career, and am raising our children with bilingual education and community involvement. I’ve been active on our County Commission for Women & Girls and Measure X Community Advisory Board. My skills are unique to the council, but not to those of us doing the work in our neighborhoods to make Concord better for our families. I’d be honored to have your vote for City Council.
https://www.instagram.com/denaabcommunity/
Concord gave my family a place to build a future, and I am running for City Council to make sure more families have that same opportunity.

I came to the United States from Peru with determination, a work ethic, and the belief that service to others matters. Today, I am a husband, father, small business owner, and healthcare leader who is proud to call District 3 home.

As Founder and CEO of Empower Minds ABA, I work with children with autism and their families throughout Contra Costa County. That experience has shown me how important it is for leaders to listen, respond with compassion, and turn concerns into action.

My community service has also focused on jobs and economic opportunity. Through the Hispanic Chamber of Commerce of Contra Costa County and the County Workforce Development Board, I have helped support local businesses, connect residents with training, and create pathways to meaningful employment.

On the City Council, I will focus on neighborhood safety, clean and well-maintained public spaces, responsible budgeting, support for small businesses, and balanced growth that protects Concord’s character while preparing us for the future.
I am grateful to have the support of Senator Tim Grayson, Assemblywoman Anamarie Avila-Farías, members of the Concord City Council, and local police officers.

I am running because public service should be practical, respectful, and focused on results. I will show up, listen, work hard, and put District 3 and Concord first. I would be honored to earn your vote.

I was born and raised in Concord. I’m from a family of immigrants who started with nothing. Just when they started to prosper, they were unjustly interned during WWII and forced to start over again. For them, hard work and a community that helped each other weren’t ideals–they were a way of life. That history shapes how I lead: serve the community, prioritizing those who need it the most.

I believe in keeping our residents safe. We deserve timely emergency response and neighborhoods where people feel secure. Our current crisis preparedness is uncertain, and that must change. We also urgently need to improve street safety, especially along the Monument corridor.

I believe in a green future. I will fight to protect and enhance our green space. We also owe it to our children to leave the planet better than we found it. Green is also the color of prosperity, starting with good schools for our children.
I’m a retired Air Force Lt. Colonel. I hold a Doctorate in Finance, a Master’s in Systems Management, and a BS in Electrical Engineering from UC Berkeley. I’m not afraid of complex problems.
Please contact me through: www.votedonseta.com
My name is Aeysha Corio, and I am asking for your vote for Concord City Council.
A City Councilmember needs to be present, accessible, and a problem solver. As Concord continues to change, we need a leader who understands our needs and makes sure we are represented.

We need our own representative who will keep our community safe. We need our own representative who will clean up blight and vacancies. We need our own representative who works well with all stakeholders. And we need our own representative who will be our advocate when it comes to fixing potholes, easing traffic congestion, or dealing with the unknown issues we will face in the future.

My track record as an effective representative has led to numerous endorsements, including the majority of the current Concord City Councilmembers, County Supervisor (and retired Concord Police Officer) Ken Carlson, the Contra Costa Deputy Sheriffs Association, IBEW Local 302, and many more.

Currently, I am a Planning Commissioner, a small business owner, and an active community volunteer serving on numerous Boards such as the John Muir Community Health Fund, and managing the annual Thanksgiving Turkey Drive.
I know what people here care about because I work alongside all of you to solve these problems every day.

To solve our problems City Councilmembers need to be accessible, so I encourage you to reach out to me at [email removed], through my website at AeyshaCorio.com, or on my Facebook or Instagram pages. I humbly ask for your vote. Thank you.
Four years ago, I asked for your trust. I promised independent leadership that puts Concord residents first. I kept that promise.

As Mayor, it’s been an honor to lead a city making real progress. As a frontline healthcare worker caring for kids with heart disease, my work has taught me the importance of listening and earning trust.
I believe that when our children and seniors are doing well, our community is doing well.

I stood up for Concord by voting to drop Seeno and get the Concord Naval Weapons Station project back on track with a trusted partner delivering union jobs, affordable housing, regional and city parks, and restoring Mt. Diablo Creek.
That vote showed I’m willing to stand up to special interests for Concord residents.
I lead the City’s Homeless Strategic Plan Working Group, identifying practical solutions that contributed to a significant reduction in homelessness.
I support thoughtful growth that protects neighborhoods, balanced housing, renter protections, traffic solutions, bike and pedestrian safety, and a new library.
My priorities are safe streets and neighborhoods, maintaining our roads and parks and essential services, responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars, and a strong local economy.

Concord resident since 1988. Longtime community and faith-based volunteer. Elected to the Concord City Council in 2022. Appointed Mayor by my colleagues in 2026. Proud AFSCME 3299 union member; formerly with National Union of Healthcare Workers (NUHW). Recipient of Save Mount Diablo’s 2024 Mountain Star Leadership Award.
I listen. I do my homework. I show up. I make thoughtful, independent decisions that put Concord residents first.
I respectfully ask for your vote on November 3.
LauraForConcordCityCouncil.com

Our family has called Danville home for nearly 15 years. We chose this community for its values and quality of life, and now, with two children in high school, my commitment to preserving and enhancing the Town of Danville is stronger than ever.

For over 27 years, I served as a law enforcement professional in Contra Costa County, including over 24 years in the San Ramon Valley. I advanced through roles as a Deputy Sheriff, Police Officer, and Detective to SWAT Team Commander, School District Liaison, Community Outreach Coordinator, and ultimately, spending my final three and a half years as a Chief of Police, retiring in December 2025.

Today, I am a small business owner, Public Safety Ambassador for Longeye, Inc. In 2023, after the loss of my husband I was emotionally and financially depleted, left with only one cent. In my deepest moments of despair, I was reminded of God’s presence and that I was not alone. My daughter and the city of Pinole welcomed me in.

I bring 32 years of public service experience, including 15 years dedicated to direct community support. My faith has taught me to lead with compassion and empathy, to listen without judgment, and to honor each person with respect.

I am running for Pinole City Council to advocate for children with special needs, parents seeking support, teachers in need of resources, seniors who deserve to age in place, families living one emergency away from homelessness, and future homeowners striving to afford a down payment.

My priorities include responsible fiscal stewardship, safe neighborhoods, thriving local businesses, expanded housing opportunities, and meaningful partnerships among schools, nonprofit organizations, faith communities, and city government.
I will trust in God and the community for guidance, I have learned the importance of listening, and stand ready to serve the City of Pinole with faith, empowerment, compassion.

As your incumbent City Councilmember, I respectfully ask for your vote to continue serving the City of Pittsburg. As a longtime resident deeply involved in our community, city development, and local government, I remain committed to building a safer, stronger, and more prosperous Pittsburg for future generations.

During my time on the City Council, I have worked to maintain fiscal responsibility through balanced budgets, attract new businesses that create local jobs, and support investments that strengthen our community. I have partnered with our Police Department, schools, nonprofits, and community organizations to enhance public safety, improve quality of life, and expand opportunities for residents. I remain committed to supporting local labor, green growth, and services for youth, seniors, and veterans.

My experience includes serving as former Chair of the Planning Commission, a union UFCW Local 5 member and shop steward for 36 years, Board Member of the Sierra Club Delta Group, current Chair of the East Contra Costa County Habitat Conservancy, Board Member of MCE, and member of the Green Empowerment Zone Governing Board.

These leadership roles have prepared me to make responsible decisions that balance economic opportunity, environmental stewardship, and sound financial management. Together, we have made meaningful progress, and I am committed to continuing Pittsburg’s positive momentum while preserving the values that make our city a wonderful place to live, work, play and raise a family.
I would be honored to earn your vote.

I’m running for Pittsburg City Council because I love this community, and I believe Pittsburg deserves a strong, independent voice someone who listens to residents, asks the hard questions, and puts Pittsburg first.

Pittsburg is my lifelong home. I was born and raised here, and my family’s roots in this community go back generations. This is more than a city I live in it’s the community that shaped me, my family, and who I am today.

I’m a full-time mother, wife and homeowner, and being a mother has made me think deeply about the future we are creating for our children. I want to help build a Pittsburg where the next generation has opportunity and a reason to be proud of where they come from.

My professional background includes banking, compliance, business consulting, startups, acquisitions, sales, logistics, and operations. As a former banking Compliance Officer and business leader, I’ve learned the importance of oversight, accountability, responsible decision-making, and asking the right questions. l’ve led teams, managed budgets, improved operations, and worked with diverse stakeholders to solve complex problems.

I’m not running because I want to be a politician. I’m running because I believe residents deserve to be heard. I will advocate for transparency, accountability, responsible growth, and meaningful resident participation.
I’m ready to serve the community that has always been home with my head high, my heart in the right place, and Pittsburg always in mind.
C.C. Cardinalli-Macaluso

Pittsburg raised me. I graduated from Pittsburg High. My grandfather started our family real estate business in 1946, my dad brought it to Pittsburg in the 1970s, and I run it today on Railroad Avenue. My wife and I are raising six kids in this town because we believe in Pittsburg.

Our city faces a five million dollar deficit, cutting the things that make Pittsburg home: Buchanan Pool, youth programs, Small World Park. A data center beside people’s homes, a school, and a church. We already lost Target, Bombardier, and the steel mill. You cannot cut your way to a thriving city. You grow your way there.

Growing Pittsburg is what I have done my whole career. As CEO of the Pittsburg Chamber of Commerce, I helped our small businesses survive COVID and reach every relief dollar available. I served on the Planning Commission, on the citizens committee overseeing your Measure P tax dollars, and on the school district bond oversight committee. I am a past president of Pittsburg Rotary.

My priorities are simple. Grow the tax base so we can fix our roads and keep our pool open without raising your taxes. Protect services for youth and seniors. Beautify the gateways to our city. Make city hall ask residents before big projects are approved, not after.
I have spent my life betting on Pittsburg. I am asking for one of your three votes.
Wolf Croskey
www.vote4wolf.org

My name is Amhari Perkins, and I am honored to be a candidate for Pittsburg City Council. I am a wife, mother, healthcare professional, and proud Pittsburg resident who believes our city deserves leadership built on transparency, accountability, and community partnership.

For more than a decade, I worked in healthcare, where I learned the value of listening, collaboration, ethical decision-making, and advocating for people when it matters most. Those experiences taught me that the strongest leaders bring people together, rely on facts, and make decisions with integrity and compassion.

Like many residents, I became more involved in local government because I saw how important community participation is in shaping Pittsburg’s future. I have worked alongside neighbors to increase civic engagement, encourage respectful dialogue, and ensure residents are informed and involved in decisions that affect our neighborhoods.

If elected, I will prioritize transparent government, responsible economic development, fiscal responsibility, public safety, environmental stewardship, and meaningful public engagement. I believe growth should strengthen our community while protecting the quality of life that makes Pittsburg a wonderful place to live, work, and raise a family.

As a mother raising my children here, I have a personal investment in the future of our city. I will always approach every decision by asking what is best for our residents today and for future generations.
I would be honored to earn your trust and your vote. Together, we can build a Pittsburg that is transparent, inclusive, financially responsible, and better for the future.

Pauline Johnson.designation: I’m Pauline Johnson, and I’m a wife, mother, and proud Pittsburg homeowner.
paragraphs: Our city approved a 350,000 square foot data center in 2024. Notice went to residents within 400 feet, so the school 500 feet away found out this year with the rest of us. This year, we also uncovered the budget is short five million dollars, with cuts ahead. Our library is now closed Mondays. A million dollars left this city in a phishing scam.

In June, I did something about it. The data center documents ran thousands of pages, English only. You deserve to know what’s happening in your own backyard. So I used my engineering background to build a four-language website, then took it further: flyers to thousands of homes, community meetings, council sessions.
That work became revealing: We asked for a pause, time to learn and have a real voice before moving forward.

That’s why I’m running: to give residents a vote in the room, not just a comment card. As councilmember, I’ll push for smart growth that fits our current zoning and includes Pittsburg’s union workers, data-driven decisions residents can hold us accountable to, departments showing their work quarterly, roads like Leland fixed instead of deferred, and real notice before decisions are made, not after, because the legal minimum isn’t enough.
Residents have a vision for our city’s future. It’s on the city to capture it, so we grow together.

Pittsburg has always been home. As a fifth generation Pittsburg High School family, I grew up learning that strong communities are built by neighbors who care for one another and leaders who show up, listen, and work together to solve problems.

I am honored you have chosen me to serve as your mayor and councilmember. Professionally, I have spent more than 20 years leading teams, solving complex challenges, and building partnerships that strengthen organizations and communities. Those experiences reinforced my belief that consistent leadership, thoughtful decision-making, transparency, and collaboration produce the best results for everyone.

Together, we have made Pittsburg stronger, investing $202M in roads and infrastructure, $11M in parks, and $6M in community facilities to meet our city’s growing needs. I am running for re-election because our progress is real, but the work is not finished. Pittsburg’s best days are still ahead.

I remain committed to making Pittsburg a city where it’s affordable for families to live, businesses grow, neighborhoods stay safe, and infrastructure keeps pace with growth. I continue to demand greater transparency, access to information, and community engagement on major projects and decisions.

I am honored to be endorsed by local leaders and workers, and would be honored to earn your vote so we can keep building a stronger Pittsburg together. Please contact me anytime at mailto:[email removed]. Thank you!
My name is Alvin Nelson, and I am running for Pittsburg City Council because our residents deserve transparent, accountable, and responsive leadership that puts our community first.

I am a Human Resources Professional with over 20 years of experience as a business leader, a husband, father, and proud Pittsburg resident. My career has been built on solving difficult problems, listening to people, managing resources responsibly, and holding organizations accountable. I also serve my community through volunteer leadership and neighborhood advocacy.

I do not support data centers in Pittsburg. I will advocate for an immediate moratorium on new data center applications and future approvals. I will oppose Phases 2 and 3 of the proposed data center development and support giving Pittsburg voters a direct voice before any future expansion moves forward. Major development decisions should be transparent and include meaningful public input.

My priorities also include safer neighborhoods, well maintained parks and streets, responsible spending, reliable public services, economic opportunities for residents and local businesses, and a City Hall that listens and responds to the people it serves.

Residents should never feel ignored when decisions affect their families, neighborhoods, and quality of life. You deserve leaders who ask tough questions, communicate openly, and are accountable for their decisions.
If elected, I will listen, lead with integrity, and put Pittsburg residents first.
I respectfully ask for your vote for Pittsburg City Council on November 3, 2026.

My public service began with the Navy. I used Veteran benefits to graduate from SFSU Paralegal Program and to attend Oakland College of Law. I did a Paralegal Internship at Oakland City Attorney’s Office. A Pittsburg resident for 31 years, I have served on several Boards/Commissions. First at Stoneman HUD Housing for nine years. Beginning as Chair of the Food Service program, then Vice President, then in 2024 as the first minority woman Board President. I‘m Afro-American/Native American. I’m proud of my rich and diverse heritage. My Great Grandfather was a Court Interpreter for Native Americans for Federal Judge Robert L. William’s Courtroom.

My community service is also diverse: Chair of Pittsburg Community Advisory Commission, PUSD Student Attendance Review Board, East Contra Costa NAACP, Contra Costa Racial Justice Oversight Board (Criminal Diversion), 2nd Vice Chair Pittsburg Elks Lodge #1474, Vice Chair Fifty Plus Club, Contra Costa Council on Aging (Housing Committee) and Vice Chair BART Police Civilian Review Board. My Environmental groups include: 350 Contra Costa Action (including Healthy Homes Project), 350 Bay Area, Sierra Club, and a graduate of Shoreline Academy. As a Councilmember on Metropolitan Transportation Commission/Association of Bay Area Governments, I address issues related to Land Use, Housing, Environmental Quality and Economic Development.
I have the experience and passion to strongly advocate for Youth, Seniors, the Environment, Affordable Housing, Transportation solutions, Public Safety , and Economic Growth. Your Chance To Be Heard.

Carolynne Born is a retired Communications and Public Relations professional whose achievements have generated awareness and support for grassroots ballot measures and corporate initiatives. She fosters pride among residents/employees, respect in the community, insight among the media, and support from stakeholders.

She is now a small business operator in pet care and advocacy, serving Central and East County. As a candidate for Pittsburg City Council, Carolynne seeks to improve citizen involvement in decision-making, influence and Quality of Life, especially as it relates to seniors, families, environmental impact, and community development. I would welcome expanded services for our seniors, such as meals and life-affirming activities.

I would like to see more community involvement at the beginning of any development project to ensure fully informed citizens. The proposed Data Center creates both economic opportunity and environmental challenge for our community. It stands as the crucial moment for Pittsburg citizens to band together and stand united in compromise and compassion. I hope to lead the way toward that compromise and create a Win-Win for our citizens. I look forward to meeting you all along the campaign trail.

I have lived in Contra Costa County since I was 5 years old, from Concord to Bay Point and now Pittsburg since 2006. I graduated from Concord High School, where I received the Principal’s Award and was elected President of the first Latinos Unidos Club. I helped organize the school’s first multicultural event, worked with students on conflict resolution, and organized a university field trip.

I enrolled at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo in Aeronautical Engineering and served on the Student Body Board of Directors. After major cuts in aerospace, military, and NASA programs following the fall of the Soviet Union, I changed my major to History and studied abroad in Mexico City for a year. After earning my BA in History, I taught for three years as a substitute and later as a World History teacher.

I am happily married and a father of three. Today, I own a successful business, employ local workers, and help clients protect their income, assets, and investments. I am a past President of the Contra Costa Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, current President of the Pittsburg Rotary, and Treasurer of United Latino Voices of Contra Costa County.
I will work to reduce theft, violence, graffiti, and vandalism, invest in our residents and future generations, and protect Pittsburg’s quality of life.
Stop the Pittsburg Data Center!
More info: WhiteEagle.info
Hi, I am Angel Rodriguez, and I am running for Pittsburg City Clerk.

I believe our City deserves a City Clerk who is transparent, accessible, and prepared to meet the needs of a growing community. The City Clerk’s office is more than an administrative function; it is how the public interacts with their local government. Every resident should have confidence that their government is open, responsive, and accountable.

As a Certified Municipal Clerk, with over twelve years in government serving the public, I understand the importance of accuracy, efficiency, and integrity. I will bring a modern approach to the office by embracing technology, improving public access to information, and ensuring that every resident can easily engage with their local government.

Our City can benefit from a new generation of leadership. Fresh perspectives and new ideas are essential to keeping Pittsburg moving forward. I respect the work that has come before, and I believe it is time to build on that foundation with energy, innovation, and a commitment to greater transparency.
I believe wholeheartedly the data center should not have been such a surprise to the community.

I will be a City Clerk who listens, communicates openly, and puts the public first. Together, we can strengthen trust in our local government by making City Hall more responsive and connected to the people it serves.
I would be honored to earn your vote and the opportunity to serve the residents of Pittsburg as your next City Clerk. https://sites.google.com/view/angel4pittsburgcityclerk/home
When it comes to City Clerk, there’s only one right lane. And that’s Melaine.

I am proud to be a candidate for Pittsburg City Clerk and to offer nearly 20 years of service to the community I proudly call home. I grew up in Pittsburg, graduated from Pittsburg High School in 1994, met my husband here, and raised our three sons here. Pittsburg is not simply where I live. It is where my family, values, and commitment to public service took shape.

As a Certified Municipal Clerk (CMC), California Professional Municipal Clerk (CPMC), and the current Director of City Clerk Services for the City of Pittsburg, I know the office, understand how City Hall works, and remain focused on the people it must serve. The City Clerk safeguards public records, supports transparent elections, helps residents access government, and ensures actions are accurate and accountable. My experience in records management, legislative processes, election administration, council support, public communication, and organizational leadership prepares me to lead from day one.

I will lead with integrity, impartiality, professionalism, and respect, while making the office more accessible, responsive, and worthy of your trust. Pittsburg has given my family so much. I am ready to keep giving back, and to keep our City Clerk’s Office moving in the right direction, forward!
I have served as your elected Clerk for 20 years, and hope to continue for the next four years. Pittsburg needs a seasoned Clerk to navigate the administration of all democratic processes.
The City Clerk does not make policy; however, the Clerk’s responsibility is to ensure records, resolutions, ordinances, and minutes accurately reflect policy that City Council adopts.

I stay current on education sessions that inform colleagues of proposed and new laws. State directives tasking the Clerk to administer are continuing every year. The constantly changing world of technology makes it imperative that the elected City Clerk stays up-to-date with new practices and innovative ideas to assist and guide the public in understanding the role of local government.

During my tenure, I served as the Election Officer in 10 election cycles, instituted paperless agendas, webcast of City Council meetings, and broadcast of meetings on the City’s website and local CCTV stations. I also guided staff to become more efficient in responding to public records requests well within the mandated 10-day response period and also effected improvements to the Council Chamber making it more user friendly for staff and residents. I believe in full transparency for all city functions.

As a Certified City Clerk and Master City Clerk, and as the compliance officer for federal, state, and local statutes, including the Political Reform Act, the Brown Act and the Public Records Act, I am well qualified to continue this responsibility.
I appreciate your vote.

I am seeking re-election to the Pleasant Hill City Council, having proudly served as your Mayor and City Councilmember. Throughout my service, I have approached every decision with a simple philosophy: providing pragmatic solutions to today’s challenges while thoughtfully preparing Pleasant Hill for tomorrow.
I believe our responsibility is to preserve the qualities that make our city special while making smart investments that strengthen our future.

As California cities face growing fiscal pressures, I believe our greatest responsibility is to balance responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars with thoughtful investments that strengthen our local economy and sustain the high-quality services our residents rely on. Experience matters when making these difficult decisions.

I remain committed to supporting local businesses, investing wisely in infrastructure, protecting public safety, and preserving the strong sense of community that makes Pleasant Hill such a wonderful place to live, work, and raise a family.
I would be honored to earn your vote and continue serving Pleasant Hill with integrity, experience, and a steadfast commitment to building a strong, sustainable future.

My name is Jason Seto, and I am running for City Council for District 3 because I believe Pleasant Hill residents deserve safe neighborhoods, transparent government, and an active voice in the decisions that affect their daily lives. My commitment is to be an open ear for every resident.

I have been privileged to call Pleasant Hill home my entire life. I attended Sequoia Elementary School, Sequoia Middle School, College Park High School (Go Falcons!), and Diablo Valley College, where I studied history and political science before transferring to UCLA (Go Bruins!). I also grew up playing AYSO soccer, Upward basketball, PHBA baseball, Warriors lacrosse and swimming for the Pleasant Hill Aquatics Swim Team.

While at DVC, I had the honor of interning for several public offices, including County Supervisor Ken Carlson’s office in the spring of 2024. For the past two years, I’ve served on the Pleasant Hill Police Department Chief’s Advisory Panel, where I have heard firsthand the public safety concerns facing our city and advocated to strengthen communication between the community and law enforcement.

These experiences inspired my passion for public service. As your Councilmember, I will work to promote public safety, fiscal responsibility, transparent government, economic growth, support for local and small businesses, and meaningful community engagement. I believe government works best when it values the voices of the people it serves. I invite you to share your concerns with me; I am here to listen and ready to serve.
Thank you, and God bless you!

I am honored to ask for your vote to continue serving on the Pleasant Hill City Council. Pleasant Hill has been my family’s home since 1998, and for nearly twelve years I have worked to protect the qualities that make our city special.

During my time on the Council, I have been proud to help advance projects and policies that strengthen our city. I supported Measure K, which has funded critical road, storm drain, and infrastructure improvements. I helped guide the new Pleasant Hill Library from vision to reality, creating a modern, welcoming, net-zero community resource for residents of all ages. I have also worked to support local businesses, maintain essential city services, promote inclusion, and keep Pleasant Hill financially responsible.

I am also proud to represent Pleasant Hill and Contra Costa County regionally through the Contra Costa Transportation Authority and as chair of the Metropolitan Transportation Commission. I bring connections and experience in Sacramento and Washington DC to help work to improve the significant mandates that impact our city and community from housing to transportation.

If re-elected, I will continue working to preserve Pleasant Hill’s small-town character while planning responsibly for the future. My priorities include maintaining safe and well-paved roads, strengthening fiscal sustainability, supporting local businesses, implementing thoughtful housing policies, and ensuring that every resident feels welcome and heard. I am grateful for the trust residents have placed in me, and I would be honored to earn your vote so I can keep working for a strong, inclusive, and financially sound Pleasant Hill.
Please visit [email removed].
When did your City Councilmember last ask: “How can I be of service?”

I ask that question every day. As a medical doctor, I ask it when a patient walks through my door. Drawing on my civil engineering degree, I ask it when an intersection is unsafe or a housing development is poorly planned. As an elected Director of the Pleasant Hill Recreation and Park District, I ask it when a park needs maintenance or a community program needs funding.
As a Vietnam War refugee, I came to this country with nothing and built a life through hard work and the kindness of community. That is why service is not just a value for me. It is personal.

My career and community service are defined by solving problems and serving people. I will put new housing in areas that make sense and don’t disrupt established neighborhoods. I will protect our parks and open spaces. I will support local businesses that make District 4 home. I will make our streets safer. And I will hold City Hall accountable to you.
I’m running a clean campaign. No political parties. No endorsement deals. No PAC money. No outside influence.
I am asking for your vote to protect what makes Pleasant Hill special. How can I be of service?
Learn more at DrQuyTran.com.

As Mayor I will deliver what Richmond residents deserve, including safer neighborhoods; better jobs; healthier air, land and water; affordable housing; and equal protection regardless of immigration status.

As an experienced, two-term Richmond City Councilmember, I have championed policies that helped our city achieve the highest level of revenue and the lowest homicide rate ever in our history. As Mayor, I can take Richmond to the next level of success.
I accept no campaign contributions from corporations, fossil fuel interests, city contractors, or developers. Being corporate-free means I work for the people, not special interests.

As a councilmember I helped secure a historic $550 million settlement with Chevron and led the fight to free Richmond from the wasteful credit default swaps pushed on us by big banks. The additional revenue I helped bring to the city put Richmond back on solid financial ground.

Now we are investing new revenue into parks, roads, public spaces, youth programs, innovative public safety programs, and needed protections for immigrant and Black communities. As mayor, I will continue to seek new sources of revenue and use city money to make improvements you can see and feel.

Because of my strong values and ability to get things done for Richmond, I have earned the endorsement of many organizations including the Sierra Club, Richmond Firefighters Local 188, the United Teachers of Richmond, SEIU Local 1021, and IFPTE Local 21. I hope I have your vote.
Richmond is at a crossroads. The decisions we make now will determine whether our city becomes safer, more prosperous, and more affordable — or whether working families continue to feel squeezed out.
I was born and raised here. This city, its resilience and its diversity shaped me. I understand Richmond, and I will bring leadership and lived experience to the office.

As mayor, I’ll focus public safety efforts on both accountability and prevention. I’ll work toward sufficient police staffing, modern training and the highest ethical standards. Safety is not just about enforcement; it’s about creating conditions where crime is less likely to occur. I’ll lead investments in mental health response, violence prevention, youth opportunity, and housing stability.

Economic strength is the foundation of community stability. We must create local jobs, support small and mid-sized businesses, diversify beyond fossil fuels, revitalize downtown, and bring bold new vision to Hilltop Mall. As former Chair of the Richmond Economic Development Commission, I understand how to bring businesses and jobs to our city.

Let’s get back to the basics: Potholes fixed. Graffiti removed. Illegal dumping addressed. Fiscal responsibility restored. Essential services protected. Pathways to homeownership and protections for renters expanded so working families can stay here and thrive.

I am endorsed by the Democratic Party, California Superintendent of Schools Tony Thurmond, State Senator Jesse Arreguín, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, Richmond City Councilmembers Soheila Bana, Jamelia Brown, and Cesar Zepeda, and over two dozen other local elected officials.
I would be honored to earn your vote.
www.Anderson4Richmond.com

While I have been on the San Pablo City Council, we have built a new City Hall, Police Headquarters/Regional Training Facility, fire station, affordable housing, parks and National Award Winning Rumrill Blvd. Complete Streets. I represent San Pablo at regional meetings and as a Commissioner on the Contra Costa Transportation Authority and West Contra Costa Transportation Commission, I have been working on a replacement of the I80 San Pablo Dam Road Interchange, soon to be under construction. Also a top priority is improving public transit for all, especially senior citizens, disabled and youth. As Chair of the West Contra Costa Integrated Waste Management Authority/RecycleMore, I am involved in outreach on recyclables and compostables, as well as tackling illegal dumping. As a Delegate to the Association of Bay Area Governments, League of California Cities and Contra Costa Mayors Conference I have gained much knowledge in best practices for cities. Our city has grown dramatically since I moved here in 1991, and I have been involved in many of those changes while on the Planning Commission and then the City Council. In 2014 I was in Denver Colorado to help San Pablo win the All-America City Award. I have worked on helping San Pablo remain fiscally responsible, maintain public safety, provide services to all residents and will continue to do so. My goal is to build more housing, attract new business and continue to make a more vibrant San Pablo.

San Pablo is the community that raised me. Growing up here, attending West Contra Costa Unified schools and Middle College at Contra Costa College before earning a Bachelor of Science in Economics from SJSU taught me that strong communities are built by investing in people.

Working in the County Supervisor’s Office, I helped connect residents with essential resources through responsive local government. At the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office, I strengthened collaboration between government and the community while informing public policy and legislative priorities. Today, my work expanding affordable homeownership opportunities and connecting families with resources has illustrated why every resident deserves a stable future in the community they call home.

As your Councilmember, I will focus on expanding affordable housing and pathways to homeownership, strengthening responsible public safety through accountability and community partnership, and creating lasting economic opportunity by building a stronger pipeline from West Contra Costa Unified School District to Contra Costa College so more local students can access sustainable careers and choose to build their futures here in San Pablo.

San Pablo has always been more than where we live, it’s home. We share a responsibility to make decisions today that ensure opportunity for generations tomorrow. Together, San Pablo will be a city where working families can afford to stay, small businesses can succeed, and young people have pathways to opportunity close to home.
I would be honored to earn your vote.
www.CadenForSanPablo.com
It has been an honor to serve the residents of San Pablo as your Councilmember and current Mayor. I respectfully ask for your vote to continue working on behalf of our community.

With more than 30 years of experience in accounting, finance, and nonprofit management, I bring a practical, fiscally responsible approach to every decision. My priority has always been protecting taxpayer dollars, promoting transparency, and ensuring the City remains financially strong while investing in the services residents depend on.

During my time on the City Council, I have worked to strengthen public safety, support local businesses, improve our neighborhoods, enhance parks and public spaces, and encourage responsible economic development that benefits our entire community. I believe in asking thoughtful questions, making informed decisions, and listening to the voices of our residents before acting.

San Pablo is a diverse and resilient community with tremendous potential. As your representative, I will continue advocating for safe neighborhoods, responsible budgeting, quality city services, opportunities for youth and seniors, and a vibrant local economy that supports families and small businesses.

Serving our community has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. I remain committed to leading with integrity, accountability, and respect while working collaboratively to build an even stronger future for San Pablo.
I would be honored to earn your vote and continue serving our community.

My family’s story is rooted in West Contra Costa County. They came to Richmond in the 1920s where they found opportunities and success. My parents and siblings lived in Atchison Village until 1971 when my parents purchased a home in San Pablo, where I grew up and attended school. I have continued to live in San Pablo.

I retired from the USPS after 38 years of service. I am the secretary for the American Postal Workers Union Local 78, and a volunteer/secretary for the San Pablo Historical Society. I am running for San Pablo City Council because this is my community, and I care about families, seniors, workers, students, and business owners. I believe that our local government should treat everyone with dignity, respect, and respond with care.

My priorities are safe and clean neighborhoods, housing affordability, education, and economic development. Safety starts in our city with trust, prevention, visibility, and community-centered solutions. We also need compassionate and practical approaches to housing insecurity. I want San Pablo to create local jobs, support businesses, and attract responsible investors and investments.

I believe no neighborhood should carry the burden of pollution without transparency and accountability. I want a stronger partnership with WCCUSD and Contra Costa College, to ensure all San Pablo children get the best possible education. I want residents to feel ownership and pride in our city through beautification programs. I am stepping up and with your vote, I look forward to serving on the San Pablo City Council.
My name is Mark Armstrong, and it has been my privilege to serve San Ramon residents since 2021.

I was initially appointed to fill a City Council vacancy and was subsequently elected Mayor by San Ramon voters in 2024. I am seeking re-election because I believe our city benefits from experienced, steady leadership that prioritizes protecting the quality of life residents value most.

Today, one of the greatest challenges facing San Ramon is balancing the State of California’s housing mandates with the need to protect the neighborhoods that residents have worked so hard to build. While we cannot ignore these mandates, we can decide where growth makes the most sense.

Residents don’t expect City Hall to control every challenge coming from Sacramento—but they do expect their local leaders to make the best possible decisions for San Ramon. That is why San Ramon has focused much of its required housing in the City Core, repurposing underutilized office buildings and helping protect established neighborhoods, parks, open space, and community character while planning responsibly for the future.

San Ramon has earned its reputation as one of California’s most desirable communities through thoughtful planning, a focus on public safety, excellent city services, beautiful parks, and engaged residents. Preserving those strengths requires ongoing attention and responsible leadership.

Today, cities across California face significant challenges. Inflation and rising costs continue to strain municipal budgets. Residents rightly expect their city government to maintain excellent services while exercising fiscal discipline and planning responsibly for the future.

These challenges cannot be solved by rhetoric or by assigning blame. They require experience, sound judgment, and a commitment to collaborate on practical solutions. I believe the best solutions come from listening carefully, respecting different viewpoints, and bringing people together to solve problems.

I support policies that strengthen public safety, preserve our parks and open spaces, support local businesses, and ensure that new development is accompanied by appropriate infrastructure and city services.

My years on the City Council and as Mayor have prepared me to lead through these complex issues and make difficult decisions. My commitment is simple: protect our neighborhoods, keep San Ramon financially strong, preserve our exceptional quality of life, and ensure that future generations enjoy the same community we are proud to call home.
I respectfully ask for your vote and the opportunity to continue serving as your Mayor.
For more information, please visit Armstrong4SanRamon.com.
Thank you for your support.

A city thrives when its leadership is proactive, compassionate, and focused on the well-being of its families. We are fortunate to live in a beautiful, vibrant city, but to protect our quality of life, we need a clear, responsible vision for the future.
I am running for Mayor to deliver that vision. My life’s mission has been defined by service, grit, and executive leadership, and I am ready to put that experience to work for you.

Driven by the values of the immigrant experience, in 2009 San Ramon became my home, and I have dedicated my career to serving this community. My background combines the drive of a former professional athlete with the strategic mindset of a business owner and non-profit director. Building ElitSwim has been my life’s work—a commitment to coaching local youth and managing sports programs that support thousands of San Ramon families. Through decades of leading organizations, balancing budgets, and solving complex challenges, I know how to set big goals, control operational costs, and actually execute a plan.
