In 2024, Chirag Kathrani ran for Mayor of San Ramon because the election was initially going unchallenged. Although Chirag lost to a sitting councilmember who became mayor, the experience strengthened his commitment to public service and showed him how often community voices go unheard.

Since that election, Chirag has dedicated significant time to engaging residents and helping them participate in local government. Chirag founded the Open Governance Initiative to amplify community voices and make government decisions easier to understand. That initiative has since grown into OpGov.News, a local news organization where communities are covered by journalists who live in and understand those communities.

Through OpGov.News, Chirag and his team do more than report what happens at City Council and school board meetings. They ask questions on behalf of residents, follow up on concerns raised during public comment, and hold public officials accountable. OpGov.News now publishes hyperlocal news throughout the Tri-Valley and delivers a physical newspaper directly to residents.

Chirag believes democracy is strongest when elections are competitive and residents have meaningful choices. After analyzing previous election results, Chirag found that voter participation often declines when candidates run without opposition. That is why he has worked to engage young people, encourage community members to consider public service, and help prospective candidates understand how to run for office.
Chirag believes meaningful change can happen only when elected representatives are accessible, responsive, and genuinely willing to listen.

One clear example is San Ramon’s appeal process. In neighboring cities, the starting fee to appeal a planning decision is generally around $300. San Ramon, however, requires residents to pay an initial deposit of $2,500, and the final cost can become a financial burden. Residents should not have to spend a fortune simply to ask their elected representatives to review a government decision. Chirag will work to establish reasonable appeal fees, clear timelines, and meaningful access to the City Council.
Chirag welcomes criticism because honest criticism helps public officials learn, improve, and remain accountable. He will listen respectfully, including when there is disagreement.
Chirag is running to represent you—and only you—not political establishments or special interests.
I am always looking for inputs from community members feel free to contact me my cell is (925) 435 7161 or email me at [email removed]

My 37 years as a teacher and mentor in the LUHSD district, 10 years as LEA union president, and proud parent of Heritage graduates uniquely qualify me to represent all stakeholders on the Liberty Union High School District Governing Board.

After earning my English degree and credential at UC Davis, I taught all levels of Liberty and Heritage students, from English Language Learners to AP Literature, was LUHSD Teacher of the Year, class advisor, student travel chaperone, and technical director for Heritage High School theatre.

I served as department chair, mentored student teachers, and coached new and experienced teachers as a consulting teacher for LUHSD’s Beginning Teacher Support and Assessment and Peer Assistance and Review programs.
As union president, I worked collaboratively with administration, ensuring safe, equitable working conditions and fiscally responsible contracts to attract and retain qualified educators.
I live in Discovery Bay with my husband, our children attended local K-12 schools, and graduated from UCBerkeley and Cal Poly SLO, thanks to excellent schools and educators.

Now retired, I want to help LUHSD provide academically appropriate and financially sound programs offering all students educational opportunities and socio-emotional support to prepare them for college, careers, and future independence.
Thank you for your consideration.

I am running for the Area 2 seat on the Mt Diablo Unified School District school board, because every child deserves a safe, welcoming, high quality public school that prepares them for success in college, careers, and life.
My connection to MDUSD is personal. I’m a 27-year resident of our community, a parent of four College Park High School graduates, a Veteran, a swim coach, and a Family Support Specialist.

As an active member of district school committees, PTAs, and as a student advocate, I’ve worked alongside teachers, staff, and families to support student programs, and make sure family voices are heard. This work has convinced me that strong schools are built on collaboration, respect, and a shared focus on students.

Our district must make responsible budget decisions while protecting classroom learning and the people who make our schools work. This means recruiting and retaining excellent educators and supporting student mental health, maintaining safe campuses, and expanding access to academics, arts, athletics, and career technical programs.

As an experienced leader and youth coach, I’ve witnessed how teamwork, discipline, belonging, and encouragement help our youth grow in confidence and resilience. Those same values should guide our school district. Every student should be known, challenged, supported, and given the opportunity to discover their strengths.

If elected, I will bring practical experience, a collaborative approach, and a commitment to listening – advocating for transparent government, sound fiscal managernent, and equitable opportunities for every student in Area 2 and across the district.
Vote For
www.DorothyWeisenberger.com

Our district doesn’t have an exemplary record. Less than half the students can read or do math at grade level. During the last decade these test scores have gradually gotten worse. I’m deeply concerned about these statistics and the lack of initiative towards fixing them. I’m Al Anderson, a husband, father, and lifelong resident of the county. It’s been many years since I worked as a high school teacher, but I have an active teaching credential and have substituted in MDUSD. While a vote for me probably won’t solve all the district’s problems, I’m not content with the status quo and will do my best. Here’s some concerns:

Financial: Our district overspends every year. With no changes, our savings will run out. Respect: Parents are the sole guardians of their children and their concerns should be treated with respect. Conversely, it is essential that teachers be shown respect in the classroom. One disruptive student can hurt an entire class. I favor detentions and suspensions, so teachers can teach and not be zookeepers. Phones: I favor a total ban. Phonics: This should’ve been required long ago. I support following the example of successful districts around the country and holding back third-graders who can’t read near grade level. Social Justice: Let’s ensure the kids can read and think critically before we wade into the mire of political activism.
During the 26 years I’ve lived in Area 4, I’ve also been a soccer coach, scout leader, and community theater director. See www.anderson4mdusd.org.
MDUSD faces real challenges – no one who is paying attention would say otherwise. We’re making measurable progress, and I want to keep building on it, not tear it down or turn back the clock.

My understanding of MDUSD isn’t theoretical – it is real world experience. I’ve coached, been in the classroom, volunteered, and served two terms on the MDUSD Board from 2012 to 2020, including as Board President.
It is important to have a parent’s perspective. I’m the only Board member with a current MDUSD student and all four of my kids attended MDUSD schools.

I hadn’t planned to return to the Board. But when a vacancy opened up last year, community members asked me to step forward – and I said yes, because I’m deeply committed to the success of this District.
I want to continue building on what we have accomplished together:

Improved academic outcomes districtwide, with proficiency up 3% and continued gains projected this year. Reached fair agreements with our teachers and staff to attract and retain outstanding educators. Refinanced bond measures, saving taxpayers millions. Strengthened fiscal oversight to keep MDUSD sound and accountable. Increased college readiness and expanded vocational offerings to make sure every graduate has a bright future. Expanded parent communication and engagement.
I’m proud to have the support of Congressman DeSaulnier, City Council members from Clayton, Concord and Walnut Creek and bipartisan leaders throughout the District.
MDUSD deserves a Board member who is invested in forward progress. I’d be honored to earn your vote.
Leadership isn’t about settling for good enough; it’s about leaving our schools stronger than we found them.

For the past five years, I have had the privilege of serving as an Oakley Union Elementary School District Trustee. As a special education teacher and father with children attending Oakley schools, every decision I make is personal. I want every student–including my own–to have the opportunity to succeed.

As a trustee, I believe our role is to set the vision, establish high expectations, and ensure accountability. I was proud to make Dual Language Immersion a priority for our district, leading to the launch of the program in 2025, and to support the direction that led to our award-winning Teacher Residency Program, helping attract and retain outstanding educators.

While I am proud of what we have accomplished together, our work is not finished. I remain committed to responsible budgeting, transparency, safe and modern schools, and improving student achievement. I believe our students deserve a district that never settles for good enough and always strives to be among the best elementary school districts in the state.
I respectfully ask for your vote so we can continue building stronger schools together
Safety. Community. Commitment. Integrity. Success.

My promise to Oakley… My name is Isaiah Mateas and I am running for the Oakley Union Elementary School Board of Education, Area 4 seat, because I want to serve the community I’ve been a part of all of my life. As a teacher, I know firsthand how the decisions of the Board affect our students, teachers, and school community. I am who you want to stick up for students’ rights. I am who you want to back teachers. I am a School Board member for the community, not for a resumé title.

From over nine years of educating in various spaces, from public schools to juvenile detention centers, I have seen how education impacts our community and shapes our children’s future. The world is changing quicker than we think, and OUESD needs leadership that’s ready for today’s educational challenges. I plan to maintain the excellence Oakley upholds while (1) expanding child safety nets, (2) strengthening student success through our robust Special Education programs and outreach to diverse communities, (3) fighting for teacher compensation, and (4) expanding arts education opportunities. A vote for me is a vote for your child’s future. Full stop.

Our family chose Orinda because we believe in public education and this remarkable community that supports it. Through volunteering in our children’s schools and currently serving as Co-President of the Wagner Ranch Parents’ Club, I’ve seen firsthand what families, teachers, staff, and volunteers can accomplish when we work together.
I’m running for the school board because I believe thoughtful, long-term leadership is essential to preserving what makes Orinda’s schools exceptional.

My professional career leading large organizations taught me the importance of strategic planning, responsible financial stewardship, and making decisions with transparency and integrity. Those principles will guide my decisions as a board member.

As a board member, I’ll focus on putting students first, strengthening communication and partnership with families, supporting our educators, and making long-term decisions that preserve the excellence of Orinda’s schools for future generations.

Our district’s greatest strength is the partnership between our schools and our community. My goal is to build on that foundation through thoughtful leadership, open communication, and a commitment to the families and students we serve.
I respectfully ask for your vote. To learn more, visit VoteJCforOUSD.org.

Public schools are essential to a thriving Orinda. As a mother of three (grades 12th, 8th, and 2nd), longtime school volunteer, and dedicated community advocate, I’ve built my career around supporting children and civic engagement, work that reflects both my professional commitment and personal investment in our community.

I’m running for re-election to the Orinda School District Governing Board to sustain the quality of our curriculum and schools, equipping students and parents with educational excellence. My priorities include strengthening curriculum, fostering a safe school environment that prioritizes mental health and social-emotional wellbeing, improving staff recruitment and retention, and advocating for a responsible budget. These efforts are vital to keeping Orinda a model of educational excellence.

My volunteer work in Orinda schools spans many roles: field trip driver at Del Rey Elementary, Girl Scout Troop Leader, library volunteer at Wagner Ranch Elementary, and board member of the Parents’ Club of OIS. Since being elected to the OUSD Board of Trustees in 2022, I’ve served as both board president and vice president.

Orinda needs leaders willing to tackle the challenges facing our children, families, educators, staff, and administration directly. Together, we can move OUSD forward and deliver results that matter to our students and community.

I’m honored to be endorsed by Assemblymember Rebecca Bauer-Kahan (D-Orinda, OUSD mom), along with many parents, teachers, staff, and administrators throughout Orinda. It would be my privilege to serve another four years, working to secure the brightest possible future for our children.

It has been a privilege to serve on the Orinda School Board for the past four years, and I am seeking reelection in order to continue to guide the positive progress of the District. Our schools are the foundation of the community. It is imperative to maintain the standard of excellence our city expects and to tirelessly strive to improve. I am eager to continue serving, and I have the experience and perspective to lead for another term.

During my tenure, I have remained focused on academic excellence and high-quality programming, fiscal responsibility and developing excellent teachers and staff. I am a pragmatic leader, setting high expectations and working towards improvement. My broader experience in education makes me particularly qualified. I have proudly worked as a California public school teacher and administrator. I am an experienced board member, having previously served on the boards of both a public school district and a private school. I also hold an Ed.M. in education policy and management. As a parent, I have volunteered in our schools and community in numerous capacities.

I will continue to work tirelessly on behalf of all constituents. I will keep students’ needs at the forefront, and I am committed to supporting rigorous and relevant curriculum and programming. Our teachers are at the core of our schools, and I will focus on supporting excellent educators. The school funding model is complicated. I will deploy resources carefully while advocating for adequate funding. I humbly ask for your vote.

Our democracy, economy, and way of life depend on a quality public education accessible to every student. Emphasizing academics, the arts, and social-emotional learning prepares students to become responsible citizens with meaningful opportunities. Achieving this requires flexible, responsive, and inclusive learning environments, as outlined in SRVUSD’s Strategic Directions, which I helped develop.

Electing trustees with proven leadership, experience, problem-solving skills, and compassion is essential to strong public schools. For the past 20 years, I have listened to our community, earned constituents’ trust, and helped strengthen education in SRVUSD. Today, more than ever, we need leaders with a proven record of collaborative, respectful leadership. My experience gives me the perspective to balance long-term district priorities with local solutions that serve all students.

My husband, Alec, and I have lived in San Ramon for 29 years, and our three children attended SRVUSD schools. Through service with District, PTA, and community committees, the California School Boards Association, Rotary, and Decoding Dyslexia CA, I remain closely connected to the concerns of parents, students, staff, and the community.
I am the Executive Director and a graduate of Leadership San Ramon Valley, an adult leadership development and community engagement program. Learn more about me at www.rachelhurdforSRVUSD.com.

As the daughter of a retired public school teacher and the parent of Walnut Creek public school students, I know the impact strong public schools have on our children, families, and community. That commitment led me to serve on the Board of the Walnut Creek Education Foundation for ten years, including four years as President. I bring a Master of Science in Marketing from Santa Clara University and experience in school finance, nonprofit governance, and building partnerships that strengthen our schools.

Working with volunteers, educators, district leaders, and community partners, we increased WCEF’s annual fundraising from $850,000 to more than $1.6 million. Those investments helped fund year-long elementary art, music, and science instruction and expanded elective opportunities at Walnut Creek Intermediate and Tice Creek. As President, I advocated for expanding orchestra to our elementary schools and adding additional semester-long electives at Walnut Creek Intermediate.

I am excited to bring this experience to the Walnut Creek School District Board of Education. Our district, like many across California, faces ongoing financial pressures. If elected, I will work to strengthen our long-term fiscal stability while protecting the educational opportunities that define Walnut Creek public schools. I will advocate for additional local and state funding and approach every decision with transparency, collaboration, and a focus on what is best for students. I believe our strongest schools are built when parents, educators, district leaders, local businesses, and community members work together with a shared commitment to helping every student thrive.

The best decisions for our schools come from people who show up: on campus, in classrooms, and talking directly with teachers, staff, and families. That’s true whether you have children in school today, raised kids here years ago, or simply believe strong public schools make Walnut Creek thrive.

I’m not a career politician. I’m a mom of two in the district, an MBA graduate, and a longtime classroom volunteer and PTA leader. My work in communications reinforces the same principle I live by as a parent: good decisions start with listening.

Here’s what I’ve learned: the best insight into our schools already lives inside them. Teachers, staff, and families see what’s working and what isn’t every day. Too often, board decisions rely on secondhand information rather than campus visits and direct conversations with the people doing the work. When those voices aren’t heard, trust erodes. And public trust is what keeps our schools strong for every generation in this community.

I want to change that. I’ll regularly visit every campus, build relationships with teachers and staff, and create meaningful opportunities for families to weigh in before decisions are made. That same approach applies to taxpayer dollars. Accountability means understanding how resources serve students, not just approving what’s on paper. Strong public schools benefit everyone, not just families with kids enrolled today.
With a new superintendent leading our district, this is an exciting moment for WCSD – and the right time for a board that shows up, listens, and builds trust.
Common Sense for Our Schools
I’ve spent a career solving hard problems under pressure, balancing budgets, and bringing people together — now I’m bringing that same discipline to the Walnut Creek School Board.

As a journalist, I learned to stay calm and focus on facts. In health technology, I managed full P&Ls and delivered results without waste. I watched doctors forced to see too many patients with too few resources. Providers burned out. Patients suffered.

Today I see the same pattern in education, with overloaded teachers and students who pay the price. I now use my health policy background to expand access to care, including Medicare and Medi-Cal services that help older adults and people with disabilities stay healthy and independent.

My approach is simple: I listen to the people doing the work, focus on root causes, protect the student-teacher relationship, and strengthen family connections — including grandparents and caregivers — that fight isolation and give kids wisdom and stability. And I keep a sharp eye on costs so every tax dollar delivers results.
If elected, I will apply this same discipline: careful stewardship of tax dollars, clear information for residents, and practical policies that protect our schools, home values, and community.

I am a parent of two children at Indian Valley Elementary, where I volunteer in the classroom. I also serve at our local food bank. I believe in staying close to the work and serving every student, family, caregiver, and resident.
I would be honored to earn your vote.
Read more at www.GGforBoard.com

School gives us our first glimpse of what the world looks like and shows us our place in society. The quality of our education and community shapes not only who we are, but who we think we can become. I am proud to have served the Walnut Creek School District for the last eight years on the Governing Board and I am asking for your support to continue in this role.

The board is responsible to ensure that our families and community experience schools as safe and welcoming environments where every opportunity is available so all our students can reach their fullest potential.

During my tenure, the district completed Measure D construction projects on time and on budget, and is midway through our Measure J projects that will bring our elementary campuses to the same modern standards of our middle schools. Our focus on careful planning and fiscal responsibility has allowed these projects to flourish in parallel with rising student achievement and a comprehensive wellness program that is a model for school districts across the county and the state.

Our community of students, teachers, staff and families continue to face new challenges and are constantly learning and adapting. I have worked to ensure that the board’s decision-making is student-centered with equity and belonging at the heart of our work. I will support our new superintendent to build upon WCSD’s strengths and look ahead to the future.
Thank you for your time and consideration of my candidacy.

Walnut Creek schools have been an important part of my family’s life. As the father of three daughters who have attended Walnut Creek School District schools—with one daughter still enrolled — I understand how deeply every decision made by the Board affects students, families, teachers, and our community.

I am running because I believe every child deserves the opportunity to learn, every teacher deserves our support and respect, and every parent deserves to be heard. Strong schools are built on trust, transparency, collaboration, and a shared commitment to student success.

For more than 25 years, I have led organizations by bringing people together, solving complex problems, and ensuring accountability. As a CPA, business executive, current associate board member of a credit union, and former Co-Vice President of Fundraising for the Tice Creek PTA, I helped raise more than $50,000 to support our schools because investing in our children is one of the greatest investments we can make.

If elected, I will listen with an open mind, communicate honestly, make thoughtful and responsible decisions, and always put students first. My goal is to help strengthen the partnership between families, educators, and the Board so that together we can provide every child with the education and opportunities they deserve.
It would be an honor to earn your trust and your vote.

Michael Robert McGill.designation: Director, Central Contra Costa Sanitary District, Div 2
paragraphs: It has been my honor to serve on the Central Contra Costa Sanitary District Board of Directors since 2006, including five terms as Board President. During my service, Central San has earned the National Platinum Award every year for excellence in wastewater management and environmental protection.

As your Director, my priorities are protecting public health, safeguarding our environment, maintaining reliable infrastructure, expanding beneficial use of recycled water, and keeping rates affordable through responsible financial management.
I supported pension reforms that eliminated pension-spiking abuses while continuing to attract and retain outstanding employees who provide the high-quality service our community deserves.

I am a licensed Civil Engineer with three engineering degrees from the University of Michigan and have owned and operated a successful California engineering consulting business for nearly 40 years. My experience in engineering, finance, and business management helps ensure thoughtful, fiscally responsible decisions.

My public service has included Chair, Contra Costa Workforce Development Board and Youth Committee; Trustee, National University; Chair, CALAFCO; Chair, BART Measure RR Bond Oversight Committee; Chair, JFKU; Chair, Los Medanos College Foundation.

I have championed innovative recycled water projects that conserve water, support local agriculture, and benefit our communities, including providing recycled water to a charity farm that grows fresh produce for families in need while educating young people about environmental stewardship (www.AgLantis.org).
I respectfully ask for your vote so I can continue providing experienced, independent, and responsible leadership for Central San.
www.MichaelRMcGill.com

I’m running for Director of the Contra Costa Water District because strong public agencies require thoughtful and experienced leadership, sound financial stewardship, and a clear commitment to the communities they serve.My extensive background in local government and special district administration spanning over 35 years includes complex budgeting (over $400 million), capital project oversight, human resources/employee relations and a Master’s degree in Public Administration. This experience has prepared me to help the District deliver high-quality water at the lowest responsible cost while protecting public health and the environment.

I have a long record of community service and civic leadership, including Rotary, and serving as current Chair of both the Martinez Civil Service Commission and the County Connection Advisory Board. These experiences reflect my belief in accountable and responsive government and meaningful community engagement.

I believe the District’s employees are among its greatest assets. Supporting a skilled, respected, and well-managed workforce is essential to maintaining high-quality service, meeting operational challenges, and serving the public effectively.

As Director, I will support responsible budgets, essential infrastructure investment, and accountable governance, always keeping ratepayers and community needs at the center of decision-making. I would be honored to earn your vote.
For more information: www.PicardforWater.com

Daniel T. Fitzpatrick.designation: Appointed Director, Contra Costa Water District Division 2
paragraphs: As your appointed Director for Division 2, I respectfully ask for your vote to continue serving Pleasant Hill, Martinez, Port Costa, and Concord.This district is my family’s home. My parents and my in-laws live in Martinez, and we are raising our daughter here. We need to get this right, so our neighborhoods and businesses thrive for the next generation.

As a real estate broker and attorney with a background in California water law, land use, and public-agency governance, I bring real expertise to the decisions this board makes: water rights, infrastructure, permitting, and fiscal oversight. As the owner of a small winery, I know firsthand how much our businesses depend on affordable water.

Our community deserves water that is safe, reliable, and fairly priced. I will protect our long-term water supply and keep rates fair, predictable, and transparent. I will invest responsibly in our aging infrastructure and strengthen drought resilience for our families and community. And I will support the District’s nearly 300 employees who serve you every day.
Local roots, legal training, and fiscal discipline guide every decision I make. I would be honored to continue this work, and I ask for your vote.

I am a retired professional Civil Engineer with 40 years of experience specializing in roads, utilities and other infrastructure. With the District preparing for the replacement of three key bridges on our roads in the coming years – one of the largest infrastructure efforts in its history – I believe my background will enable me to serve effectively as a Director of the DCSD.

These bridges are essential to community safety and reliable access to our homes. Throughout my career, I have coordinated successfully with the consultants and contractors this project will require, including bridge designers, structural and geotechnical engineers, landscape and CEQA specialists, and construction teams. My expertise directly supports the technical oversight and coordination needed to replace the bridges on schedule and within budget.

My experience also includes issues such as land use, zoning, land planning, property subdivision, and the construction of homes. This background would help me fulfill the Board’s additional role of representing the community as the Diablo Municipal Advisory Council (DMAC).
My wife Deborah and I love Diablo – we are members of the Diablo Country Club and we enjoy participating in community and social events.

If elected, I will focus on careful planning, transparent communication, and responsible oversight so the District can help preserve the safety, character, and quality of life of our historic and special community.

“It’s an honor and a privilege to seek election to the Diablo Community Services District Board, where I have served as a Director and Board Secretary for the past 11 months after being appointed to fill a Board vacancy.

My career has taken me through sales leadership roles at Hewlett-Packard, Microsoft, and BMC Software, where I solved mission-critical problems for global customers, managed resources wisely, and delivered excellent results. In addition, I have volunteered my leadership skills as a board member and president of Youth Homes, a non-profit supporting traumatized foster children in Contra Costa County, and as an assistant scoutmaster of Troop 36 at St. Timothy’s Church in Danville. I was awarded a Ph.D. in Chemistry by the University of Waikato, New Zealand, and completed my post-doctoral research at the University of Virginia.

My wife, Caroline, and I lived in Walnut Creek for 32 years and raised our three children there. We are the proud grandparents of four grandchildren. We were very excited to move to Diablo in 2019, a community we have always admired for its uniqueness, leafy ambience and historical character.

If elected to the DCSD Board, I will serve with integrity, transparency, and practical leadership to keep Diablo safe and well-maintained. I pledge to be responsive to residents’ needs and always put the well-being of our residents first in all decision-making.
I would be honored to receive your vote to elect me to the DCSD Board. Thank you for your support!
It is an honor to seek election to the Diablo Community Services District Board.

My husband and I have proudly called Diablo home for more than ten years. We were drawn here by the unique history, character, and strong sense of community that make Diablo such a special place to live. As a resident of one of Diablo’s historic homes, I have a deep appreciation for preserving the qualities that have made this community exceptional for generations.

Professionally, I serve as Chief Human Resources Officer at Rodan + Fields, where I lead the company’s human resources, corporate charitable giving, and corporate real estate functions. Throughout my career, I have partnered with executive teams and boards to solve complex challenges, build consensus among diverse stakeholders, and make thoughtful, transparent decisions that balance competing priorities while always keeping people at the center.

If elected, I will serve with integrity, transparency, and respect for every member of our community. I am committed to listening first, fostering civil and constructive dialogue, and helping ensure Diablo remains a safe, financially responsible, and well-maintained community while honoring its rich history and unique character.
I would be honored to earn your vote and the opportunity to serve the Diablo community. Thank you for your support.

My name is Kismat Kathrani, and I am running for Director of the Dublin San Ramon Services District because every family deserves safe and affordable water. It should never be a privilege—it is a basic right.

As a husband and proud father of two children attending UC Berkeley, I think deeply about the world we will leave to the next generation. Whenever a child turns on a faucet, their family should have complete confidence that the water is safe. Protecting that trust requires leadership, preparation, and accountability.

Our water system faces aging infrastructure, PFAS contamination, drought, and rising costs. As an engineer, management graduate, and entrepreneur, I have the experience to address these challenges. I built my businesses from the ground up without outside investors, creating thousands of jobs through discipline, innovation, and responsible financial decisions.
I also serve as President of the Bay Area chapter of ITServe Alliance, supporting technology companies and local employment.
As your director, I will prioritize fiscal responsibility, long-term water security, drought preparedness, PFAS monitoring, infrastructure modernization, and transparent decision-making.
Clean water protects our health, our families, and our future. I humbly ask for your vote and the opportunity to serve our community.
Learn more at kismatforpeople.com.

After studying Roman aqueducts in college, I saw that the quality of a town’s water infrastructure is a measure of its level of civilization. After attending the Dublin San Ramon Services District’s Water Academy, I learned about our excellent local water and wastewater management team. I am running for Director of DSRSD’s Division 2 to bring over 40 years of earth science expertise. Qualifications: B.A. in Geology (University of Texas at Austin) with an Engineering minor; M.S. in Geology (CSU East Bay); Retired Chevron Earth Scientist and Certified Petroleum Geologist; California Registered Geologist #7487; Graduate of DSRSD Water Academy.

Priorities (1) Safe Drinking Water: Protect public health through rigorous lab testing, (2) Smart Infrastructure: Use modern technology to monitor aging systems and prevent costly failures, (3) Recycled Water Leadership: Maximize our recycled water use success, with a goal of zero treated wastewater to the bay during peak landscape irrigation in the summertime, (4) Fiscal Value: Maintain high-quality wastewater services at a fair price for Division 2 residents.
I will use my professional background to keep DSRSD strong, safe, and efficient. I ask for your vote to protect our vital resources.

When elected to EBMUD in 2014, I promised to expand water conservation and recycling, replace our aging pipelines, keep water affordable, lead on climate action, and protect the Mokelumne River. I kept those promises. I secured permanent protection of the Mokelumne and expanded watershed recreation access. I put EBMUD on a path to net zero emissions by 2030, prepared us for droughts, wildfires, and power shutoffs, and nearly tripled the pace of pipeline replacement to keep our water flowing 24/7/365. I drove our efforts to reduce harmful nutrients polluting the Bay. I made our shutoff moratorium permanent, and expanded our customer assistance program, ensuring no customer loses water due to inability to pay, while keeping rates affordable for everyone. I have spent more than 40 years in public service protecting our environment and improving the lives of working people, including as California Director of Clean Water Action, where I fought for safer drinking water and Bay Delta water quality. I am a third-generation Californian, lifelong EBMUD customer, and UC Berkeley graduate in Natural Resource Economics. My endorsements include EBMUD Directors, Clean Water Action, Sierra Club, AFSCME, and many other environmental, community, and labor leaders. Please join them. See my priorities for 4 more years at www.young4water.org
This candidate has accepted East Bay Municipal Utility District’s voluntary expenditure limits.

I’m running to ensure high quality service and the lowest responsible rates to EBMUD customers, using innovative approaches and in-house staff. I’ve worked in the municipal water treatment field since age 19, in plants across the US and in Kuwait, South Korea, and South Africa, and at EBMUD for 30+ years, most recently as Manager of Technical and Emerging Issues before retiring. I was a consultant and design engineer for EBMUD’s first major water recycling plant, which provides up to 5.4 million-gallons-daily. At EBMUD, I: worked with regulators to create regulations reducing treatment cost and your EBMUD bills; obtained 2 patents for first-of-their-kind processes to recycle food waste, otherwise landfilled, producing soil amendment and power for the electrical grid, and to operate infrastructure differently, lowering rates; secured grants from government and private organizations to conduct research that saved millions in both operating and capital costs; and developed use of existing facilities to meet new ammonia regulations, instead of spending $2B on new infrastructure that would have substantially raised rates. I am a registered engineer and Grade 5 operator in California. Education: BS, CalPoly SLO; PhD, Civil/Environmental engineering, UC Berkeley; MBA-Finance, UC Davis.
This candidate has accepted East Bay Municipal Utility District’s voluntary expenditure limits.

I’m an expert, not a politician. I will bring 40 years of experience as a water resources engineer and economist (wolff4water.org/about) to make the East Bay Municipal Utility District work better for you. I’ve been the Vice Chair of the California State Water Resources Control Board, the Executive Director of the Alameda County Waste Management Authority (“StopWaste), a water and wastewater utility efficiency expert, a businessperson, and a licensed contractor. I’ve served on EBMUD and Castro Valley Sanitary District community advisory committees. I understand the problems we face, and I know that success requires listening and people skills, along with technical knowledge. Water rates have gone up steeply, and climate change is affecting water quality. But we can keep water affordable, protect water quality, improve and expand the low-income customer assistance program, use water more efficiently, and keep parks and schools green. I will represent you as we build a better water future. That’s why more than 100 elected officials, community leaders, and organizations have endorsed me (wolff4water.org/endorsements). Supporters include California Treasurer Fiona Ma, Senator Grayson, the Alameda Labor and Building Trades Councils, five EBMUD Boardmembers, including President Luz Gomez, all EBMUD unions, business leaders, and the Sierra Club. I humbly request your vote so that I may do this work for you.This candidate has accepted East Bay Municipal Utility District’s voluntary expenditure limits.

April Chan.designation: Director, East Bay Municipal Utility District, Ward 7
paragraphs: Every dollar EBMUD spends matters. I treat your money as my money. As your EBMUD Director, I exposed $279 million in undisclosed budget transfers and led efforts to bring greater transparency and accountability to EBMUD’s finances. I advocated to eliminate the 8.5% drought surcharge in 2023 because Ward 7 families shouldn’t pay more than necessary.
When a proposal threatened to turn Lake Chabot Road into a soil dump route with 100 trucks a day for 60 years, I stood with San Leandro and Castro Valley residents, and together we stopped it.

As an Alameda County Fire Commissioner, I know public safety depends on reliable water. I initiated a new accountability standard for fire hydrant inspections because dependable hydrants save lives in wildfire-prone areas. The measure passed with support from the firefighters who rely on them.
I’m not a career politician. I ask tough questions, challenge waste, and hold government accountable—even when it’s unpopular with insiders.
If you want an independent voice who protects your dollars, stands up for our communities, and delivers results, I respectfully ask for your vote.
Join Alameda County Supervisor Nate Miley, San Leandro Mayor Juan Gonzalez, and San Ramon Mayor Mark Armstrong in re-electing April Chan for EBMUD Ward 7 2026.
https://chan4ebmud.com/
This candidate has accepted East Bay Municipal Utility District’s voluntary expenditure limits.

Colin J. Coffey.designation: Board Member, East Bay Regional Park District
paragraphs: It is an honor to serve as your representative to the East Bay Regional Park District Board these last nine years. My experience on the Board, combined with my years on the Parks Advisory Committee and as a volunteer East Bay Parks Ambassador, has corresponded to great success, including the addition of new parkland for preservation of open space and wildlife habitat, and new funding for our wildfire prevention efforts.

Our East Bay Parks make life here special. They not only preserve open space and natural areas, our Parks provide families a healthy environment to connect with nature through hiking, picnicking, swimming and camping – even as our region grows and changes. My priorities are maintaining and improving parks, trails, natural areas, and open space. This includes protecting wildlife habitat and water quality, preventing wildfires, improving park bathrooms, and increasing park safety. I am proud that the EBRPD police department is close to 100% staffing.

I am proud to be endorsed by the Sierra Club, Contra Costa Labor Council, Building Trades, Congressmembers Mark DeSaulnier and George Miller (retired), Assemblymember Annamarie Avila Farias, and Contra Costa Supervisors Burgis, Scales-Preston, Gioia, and Carlson. I would appreciate your vote. www.colincoffeyforparks.com
I’m a regenerative organic farmer, healthcare innovator, and Crockett resident running for Ward 7 to transform our parks+farms into engines for public health and ecological economics.

Our regional parks & resources are our greatest preventative healthcare assets. Through my nonprofit, www.CultivatingSelf.org I’ve spent years reimagining healthcare, proving that access to nature and ecological medicine are vital to curing systemic burnout and chronic illness. I’m on the Advisory Council On Aging with Contra Costa County, supporting senior intergenerational wellbeing.

Intersecting crises in resources and public health require holistic, economic solutions. Guided by Doughnut Economics, I believe our Park District must build a resilient local economy that balances human needs with ecological boundaries. We can achieve this by expanding green workforce development and regenerative land stewardship.

Additionally, through the www.CosmicLabyrinth.world collective, I have organized disaster resilience, community eco-restoration projects, and farm infrastructure. I will bring this hands-on experience to ensure our parks foster food sovereignty, expand community gardens, and utilize indigenous land management to mitigate wildfire risks.

I’ll ensure our budget is invested transparently to create generational wealth through healthy ecosystems, accessible trails, and thriving community hubs. Let’s reimagine our parks as centers of wellness and regenerative doughnut economics.

I am seeking election to the Ironhouse Sanitary District Board because I want to help ensure the District continues providing reliable, cost-effective wastewater services while responsibly planning for the future.

The Corridon family has proudly called Oakley home for more than 20 years and we have made a point of supporting the community in any way needed. I presently serve as an Assistant Scoutmaster with Oakley Troop 152.

I have spent my career solving complex operational and engineering challenges while finding practical ways to reduce costs and improve performance. My experience in operations, engineering, quality, safety, and environmental management has taught me the value of careful planning, responsible risk management, sound stewardship, and fact-based decision-making.

As a Director, I will support responsible financial management, risk mitigation, long-term infrastructure planning, reliable public service, and transparent decision-making. I believe government works best when it plans ahead, spends wisely, and focuses on providing dependable public services. I will work collaboratively with fellow Board members and District staff to protect the interests of our ratepayers and help ensure Ironhouse Sanitary District continues to serve Oakley and Bethel Island with integrity, accountability, and common sense.
I respectfully ask for your vote.
I respectfully ask for your support in my re-election to the Ironhouse Sanitary District Board of Directors.

I was appointed to the Board in 2004 and elected by the ratepayers in 2006. This November, I will have 22 years of experience representing our community and ensuring that the interests of our ratepayers remain the District’s highest priority.

As a longtime resident, former Oakley small business owner, and current Bethel Island resident, I understand the importance of providing essential services while maintaining responsible financial management. Every decision made by the Board affects the community we serve, including my own family.

Ironhouse Sanitary District is a high-performing organization that our community can be proud of. Our dedicated employees operate three divisions that work 24 hours a day, seven days a week, collecting, treating, and safely disposing of wastewater while meeting strict state and federal environmental requirements.

Since the Water Recycling Facility began operation in 2011, the District has expanded its commitment to sustainability by providing recycled water opportunities for ratepayers while protecting our region’s water resources.
The District is also investing in its future through a new solar energy project that will provide long-term energy cost stability and help protect ratepayers from rising electricity expenses.

I am committed to continuing responsible leadership, maintaining reliable service, protecting our environment, and making decisions that serve the best interests of Ironhouse ratepayers today and for future generations.
I would be honored to receive your vote.

My name is Paschal Iwuh. I am married with four children. I am a member of the Oakley/Bethel Island community. I am very interested in seeing our community develop further and accommodate both incoming residents and businesses.

I am running to be a member of the Ironhouse Sanitary District because I have the technical and managerial experience to help move the District forward. I care about our environment, waste treatment and recycle water services. In the last year or so, I took the time to tour the Ironhouse Facility and met with the management and staff to get a full understanding of operations, environment and challenges facing the District. Also, I did ask some residents of their expectations of the District.

As an experienced engineer with more than 20 years’ experience in both manufacturing and water systems, I can bring to bear in discussions and technical agreements in collaboration with engineers. As an experienced manager of projects, people, departments and units with over 15 years’ experience, I can help the board to ensuring that our annual budgets reflect the good aims and objectives of the District so we manage costs to have a profitable business at ISD. As a committed community member in the District, I can relate to the needs of the people of the District to ensure that the ISD is a mirror image of their values, culture and needs.
I am asking for your valuable and highly esteemed vote so I can represent our District. Thanks for your time.
Sincerely,
Dr. Paschal Iwuh, PhD
The Lamorinda area has been my home since my children were small, and I love it. The safety and wellbeing of the community is of prime importance to me.
In recent years I have become increasingly aware of the fire danger in this area. As my awareness of potential fire danger grew, I came to appreciate the role of the MOFD.

MOFD was formed in 1997 by the residents of Moraga and Orinda. Its defined purpose was to use property taxes for fire protection. These taxes were allocated for fire protection by Prop 13, to be used by the communities which generated these taxes.
The voters’ pamphlets for this election are still available (see www.Steve4MOFD.info/MOFD-voter-pamphlets)
As a Director of our MOFD, I will uphold the original intent in its formation.
I have worked hard to learn about the inner workings of the district.
I want safe communities for all of us, and am willing to work very hard on behalf of this commitment.
Neighbors,

I am asking your support to become your Moraga Orinda Fire District Board member, representing Division 3. MOFD’s continued success is vital to protecting the health and well-being of our community. Its current strong position is a tribute to years of hard work in the District and our broader community. Maintaining this high level of readiness requires a continuous commitment of time, money and effort, an investment in our community’s safety that cannot be neglected. In the near term, the implementation of Zone Zero regulations statewide is still a work in progress. Once the state puts its implementation plan in place, MOFD will need to manage the transition for our area. A new fire station is needed to replace Station 41, as its current design is no longer able to fully support MOFD operations. Success depends on MOFD and our community working together in a collaborative and cost-effective manner. As a Board Member I will work to support MOFD’s engagement in these key areas.

As a 28-year resident of MOFD Division 3, I am willing and able to provide the oversight needed to assist MOFD in its next phase. I am Past President and current Treasurer of the Rotary Club of Orinda and also have been Assistant Governor for the 5 Rotary Clubs in our area. After completing a PhD in Immunology, I worked in discovery and development of vaccines for Merck, Chiron and Novartis. Later I joined the nonprofit PATH where I directed a program to assist developing country vaccine manufacturers. Finally I served as President of the nonprofit Global Healing, which works to improve the quality of pediatric care in low-income countries.

I also am retired from 30 years’ service as a US Army Medical Service Corps officer, both Reserve and Active, with deployments to Operations Desert Shield/Desert Storm and Iraqi Freedom 2. My final assignment before retiring was as Deputy Commanding General, 3rd Medical Deployable Support Command, Ft. Gillem, GA. Providing emergency medical transportation is a large part of MOFD’s mission and also a vital element of Army Medicine. My duties included leadership of Army medical units, including evacuation assets, at various levels of command. I believe this experience will be useful to MOFD. This military information does not imply endorsement by the Department Of War or the Department Of The Army.
I will very much appreciate your support in the coming election.

Technology is advancing fast, and that’s good news for our fire district. New tools are making fire prevention, response, and recovery smarter and more effective every year. I want to help the Moraga-Orinda Fire Protection District put those tools to work for our community.

For more than 40 years, I’ve worked in the geospatial industry, building technology that supports firefighters and first responders. I spent 28 years as an executive at ESRI, the world’s leading Geographic Information Systems (GIS) company. That experience taught me how to identify practical solutions, learn from proven approaches, and bring the right experts to the table. I’ll use that knowledge to strengthen how our District protects the nearly 38,500 residents across our 42 square miles.

Our District faces real challenges. We include areas designated as Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones, and our crews respond to more than 3,000 incidents each year. Smart planning and modern tools can help our firefighters work faster, safer, and more efficiently. I believe I can help make that happen.

I also understand the power of community. As a former board member of the Southern California Mountains Foundation, I saw firsthand how local organizations and engaged citizens can expand what our firefighters are able to do. Strong partnerships and open communication make our whole District safer.

I hold a degree in geography from UCLA and a Master’s from the University of Redlands. I moved to the LaMorinda area in 2015 and quickly found my home here. I love our access to nature, our small-town charm, and our easy connection to San Francisco. Protecting this special place is personal for me.

I’m asking for your vote so I can bring my technical expertise, board experience, and deep commitment to our community to the MOFD Board of Directors. Together, we can keep Moraga, Orinda, Canyon, and Bollinger Canyon safe for years to come.
As an Orinda resident and your Division 4 director on the Moraga-Orinda Fire District board, I ask for your support to continue the work we have started together.

We live in one of the most beautiful — and most fire-vulnerable — regions in California. The hills above us are not an abstract risk; they are our neighborhoods and our homes. As a director and Firewise Ambassador, I have worked to put science and technology to work for our safety: hands-on home-hardening assessments, and expanded defensible-space education so homes are prepared before the next Diablo wind event — not after. I also publish free, step-by-step ember-protection guides on roemerwise.com. This work is never finished, and I am committed to continuing it.

We expanded ambulance service with an innovative single role paramedic program that increased service availability while reducing the pressure on district pension obligations. We acquired a new administration building, paying cash with no interest expenses, for essential staff offices.

Fiscal stewardship is essential. MOFD is a public trust, and every dollar the district spends belongs to the taxpayers of Moraga and Orinda. I worked to bring discipline and transparency to our budgeting, and I am a consistent voice for addressing long-term pension obligations honestly — not deferring hard decisions to future boards and residents. We invested tax revenue in safe Treasury bills that increase our returns, and hired new investment advisors to manage investments to protect post employment benefits for our firefighters. Sound finances are what make good service, to our firefighters and to our community, sustainable.

I believe in a board that works. Special district governance at its best is quiet, competent, and collaborative. Directors aligned on mission — even when they disagree on specifics — accomplish far more than those focused on conflict. I will continue to prioritize respectful, productive deliberation that keeps our focus where it belongs: the safety of the people we serve.

Before my district service, I served the public as an Alameda County Deputy District Attorney. I volunteered as a MOFD Support member in radio communications, evacuation practice, prescribed burns, and support services for our firefighters on callouts. My commitment is straightforward: show up prepared, ask hard questions, listen to residents and staff, and decide based on the long-term wellbeing of this community.
I am proud to serve Moraga and Orinda, and I would be honored to continue doing so.
—Mike Roemer

As Vice Chair of the Martinez Diversity and Cultural Commission and a board member of the Contra Costa County Marathon Community Benefits Agreement Panel, I center my public service around listening to residents, advocating for equity, and ensuring transparent oversight. I am seeking your vote for Director, District 2, Mountain View Sanitary District to bring that same commitment to our vital local public infrastructure.
An avid cyclist, I experience our beautiful neighborhood street by street. I see firsthand how essential modern, clean and reliable utility systems are to our public health and local environment.
If elected, my priorities will be:
Environmental Stewardship: Safeguarding our local ecosystems through efficient wastewater treatment and environmental care.
Fiscal Oversight: Ensuring your dollars are invested wisely in proactive infrastructure upgrades and long-term reliability initiatives.
Community Transparency: Keeping board decisions open, accessible, and responsive to neighbor input.
Local service is my daily commitment to this place we call home. I respectfully ask for your vote to keep Mountain View Sanitary District strong, sustainable and accountable.
For more information, visit GwenGilkey.com

Derek M Wurst.designation: Director, Pleasant Hill Recreation & Park District
paragraphs: I respectfully ask for your vote for Director of the Pleasant Hill Recreation & Park District. During my first term on the Board, including serving as Chair, I have worked to strengthen our District by supporting initiatives that improve accessibility, safety, recreation opportunities, and community engagement. I supported the District’s diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives, ADA Plan, Security Plan, and capital improvement projects that have enhanced the accessibility and safety of our parks and facilities. I also advocated for pursuing a general obligation bond to address infrastructure needs and improve existing facilities for future generations.I believe parks and recreation are essential to the health, well-being, and quality of life of our community. As Chair, I focused on supporting innovative and diverse recreation programs, maximizing the use of existing facilities, and building stronger connections among residents of all ages. Our parks and recreation facilities are gathering places that foster community, encourage active lifestyles, and enrich the lives of children, families, and seniors alike.

If re-elected, I will continue working collaboratively with residents, District leadership, and community partners to enhance parks, recreation programs, and public spaces. I am committed to fiscal responsibility, sustainable operations, expanded public art opportunities, and strategic investments that reflect community priorities. I will continue advocating for long-term improvements identified in the District’s Master Plan while ensuring taxpayer resources are managed responsibly.
I will bring practical leadership, sound judgment, and a steadfast commitment to preserving and enhancing the amenities that make Pleasant Hill a wonderful place to live.
Thank you for your vote.

Robert \"Bobby\" Glover.designation: Director, Pleasant Hill Recreation and Park District
paragraphs: Dear Neighbors,For more than a decade, it has been my privilege to serve our community as a member of the Pleasant Hill Recreation and Park District Board, and I respectfully ask for your support for re-election.

I grew up in this community, attending Valley View Middle School, College Park High School, and Diablo Valley College. Giving back to the community that helped shape me has always been my motivation for public service.

My commitment extends well beyond Board meetings. I spent seven years coaching youth soccer with the Pleasant Hill Martinez Soccer Association, continue to coach youth softball with the Pleasant Hill Baseball Association, volunteer as an official for the Pleasant Hill Dolfins Swim Team, serve as a commissioner with the Pleasant Hill Baseball Association, and am proud to be a member of the Pleasant Hill Senior Club. These experiences keep me connected to the children, families, and seniors our District serves.

During my service, the District has invested in new community facilities, including the Community Center and Senior Center, improved parks and athletic fields, and expanded recreational opportunities that enhance the quality of life for residents throughout our District. I remain committed to fiscal responsibility, transparency, and ensuring our parks and programs continue to meet the needs of future generations.
I would be honored to continue serving our community and respectfully ask for your vote.
Thank you for your support.
Bobby Glover

Sandra Bonato.designation: Pleasant Hill Recreation and Park District, Director
paragraphs: My name is: Sandra Bonato
My occupation is: Attorney

I am honored to have served the residents of the Pleasant Hill Recreation and Park District since January 2009. I have chaired the District’s Board of Directors multiple times, including during the period when the District built three new community facilities and refurbished the ballfields at Pleasant Oaks Park. I have served on and chaired the Budget Committee for many years, a position that is integral to the needs and expectations of residents for inspiring programs, special events, and beautiful parks and facilities.

As an attorney, I am analytical and inquiring and urge fiscally prudent decision-making. I also believe in reaching for dreams. As a Board member, I want to inspire enriching programs, green parks and ball fields, sparkling pools and playgrounds, cultural, historic, art and performance opportunities, and healthy recreation and social interaction for all ages, abilities and interests.

Our District has developed a Master Plan to help the Board evaluate where it should head into the future. While we have prized buildings and fields, the District also has aging properties that must still be evaluated and addressed. We also have five acres of parkland adjacent to the Pleasant Hill library, which affords an exciting opportunity to provide even more recreational resources for our residents – and to preserve open, accessible land forever.
Much remains to be accomplished. I am honored to ask for your vote.
